Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon

📅 14 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5353 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half.
  • Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins.
  • There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half. It was muffled at first, but as the ball popped from one white shirt to another, it became louder and louder, sweeping around the stadium: here was the soundtrack for a humiliation.

“Olé! Olé! Olé!” they roared and why not? Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins. Football has become a sport that leaves people increasingly vexed, but this was a night when – for the locals, at least – it was almost a throwback.

There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.

It has been revealed that “I suppose in football you can always find something to moan about,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, said. “But this was a top-class performance.”.

Recent findings suggest that it has felt suspiciously like Newcastle’s start has been like an overstuffed plastic shopping bag, the handles straining to the point of snapping. Eventually they fell asunder. Leeds ran all over them and were too smart, slick and hungry, not to mention ruthless. No wonder Jaissle had nowhere to go.

Industry observers note that the home fans were adamant this was one of the best nights Leeds have experienced under Farke and if they were prepared to say as much, you had an obligation to listen. Forget how wretched Newcastle were, Leeds had produced a performance to enable imaginations to run wild.

Centre to it all was Ao Tanaka, with his desire to keep Leeds playing forward, but it felt wrong to talk about one man when you had the unstoppable Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who would be substituted to a standing ovation, and the ubiquitous James Justin, among others.

"He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj.

The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous fresh West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a massive evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

In a recent development, massive? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

Industry observers note that leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

Sources indicate that jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

Ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO.

Leeds were running even quicker by this point, pressing as if their lives depended on it and making tackles that were lustily acclaimed in the stands. Steur completely short-circuited in the bedlam and a ridiculous pass on the edge of his area was pounced upon by Bogle.

Out went a ball to Justin, whose cross was whipped into the penalty area, where Calvert-Lewin had climbed to get his head to it, though replays indicated his effort glanced off Bogle’s head – determining the true scorer will make for an interesting conversation.

Calvert-Lewin, at least, got the reward his efforts deserved on the cusp of half-time, spinning away from Miley and chopping inside Sven Botman before delivering the kind of finish that should make Thomas Tuchel take note when selecting his next England squad this week.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9.

The gloss, after those “olés”, was applied in the 59th minute when Noah Okafor put a realistic hue on the score, ramming in a finish in front of the Kop and leaving Newcastle open to the crudest mocking for the amount of money they have spent to resemble such a disorganised rabble.

It has been revealed that A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x.

Bazoumana Touré, at least, scored a consolation goal, but Jaissle barely flickered as it went in and the emotion belonged to Farke, who thundered on to the pitch at the final whistle and sought out his captain, Ampadu, who had erred in allowing Newcastle’s substitute to profit.

“That was an unnecessary goal to concede and I so wanted us to keep a clean sheet,” Farke sighed. “We deserved a clean sheet and I couldn’t help myself. I had to tell him because I am sometimes a perfectionist. We must try to stay humble, but we can be an outstanding team.”.

And this, for certain, was an outstanding night.

[It was brutal out there?] That’s football. That’s the Premier League. It was clear from the start and I have said it many times. We will have ups and downs and challenges all the way. Tonight we faced that challenge. It’s tough and difficult to digest. But there is a chance to learn out of that and there’s a long time until our next match at home and that is good.

It’s clear with our young squad that there will be ups and downs and you have to bring the fundamentals on the pitch against such a physical team. Leeds are so intense, we couldn’t match that physicality. There are other aspects of course but I don’t want to make excuses. We want to learn out of it and be better.

In a recent development, [Were you overwhelmed as a team?] No. If you don’t bring that physicality on the pitch, you struggle.

According to recent reports, exactly this [message to the players]. Bring your fundamentals and we build on it. [Can you bounce back from this in your next game?] Of course. [Is your confidence hit?] No.

According to recent reports, for each manager it would be a nightmare after such a game to concede so late and not have the well-deserved clean sheet. Of course I was not happy about the situation. Doesn’t take anything away from my boys who were magnificent. Terrific start with eight points but there’s never a perfect performance. There’s always something to moan about. At very rare points [in the season] I have to criticise [for conceding].

In a recent development, energy, quality, good structure, in an out of possession, which is complicated against Newcastle, In pressing them you always have to be aware of their unbelievable pace and strength in counter-attacks. We found this balance today and in the first half particularly we were dominant.

We have a good fitness level now. Need to find the right triggers to press. It’s a lot of well-structured work on the training ground. We had more chances to score tonight but overall I am very happy with our performance.

[Calvert-Lewin being praised] It is well deserved. He is in outstanding shape and plays with lots of confidence. I expect him to lead the group with some other players. His work-rate is never in doubt and to me he is one of the best strikers in the league.

According to recent reports, the ref told me at half-time that they’ve taken it off me. I didn’t know he [Bogle] was there to be fair. I just got up and went ‘Bang!’ It is what it is. I’ll take the assist!

It has been revealed that I didn’t know anything about it [being given credit for the second goal]. I said to the ref, I don’t fancy telling him [Calvert-Lewin]. To be fair he’s still raging. He’s raging with the goal but happy with the result.

It’s about having an understanding with the players around you. With Dom up there, you know he’s going to win everything so you have to get the runners around him.

Industry observers note that it’s about the rotation like today. When James Justin goes wider there’s space inside. Dom occupies two centre-backs so there’s always pockets.

Recent findings suggest that regardless of the scoreline it was a tough game physically. They’re a very good side. We take it game by game, not to get carried away. Everyone’s ambitious in their own way but we have to take it game by game.

A proper stuffing for Newcastle as Leeds continue to impress and climb up to third.

James pounces on a loose ball, dribbles infield from the right. No one bothers to close him down so he eventually has a shot, blazing over with his left from 20 yards.

Late free-kick for Leeds after Livramento bundled Aaronson over. Wilson chips from the left to the far post and Muharemovic heads it back acros goal looking for a team-mate but none had made the run.

Ampadu and Bamba collide when fighting for a loose ball but there was nothing malicious in it.

According to recent reports, newcastle corner on the left headed out by Elvedi and Barnes recovers the ball to start another attack with the 18-yard line stacked with players. When the diagonal comes back from left to right Barnes heads it behind for a goalkick.

Willock hooks a half-volley on to the roof of the net.

Newcastle are enjoying more possession but the crossing has been awful when they do get down the flanks, Touré the latest offender.

Barnes shoots down Trafford’s throat. Barnes had thrown himself down in the box moments earlier and there was a VAR check but there was nothing like the contact required to send him swan-diving on to the grass.

Wissa gets down the right and whips over a low cross but Willock’s touch was too heavy.

Recent findings suggest that there was a piece in the Athletic today saying Newcastle pivoted to Hornicek instead of pursuing Trafford again because he had a very high ceiling and was younger. He hasn’t caught much here, dropping the ball even when he chooses not to punch.

Matthias Jaissle promised high intensity, high octane, front foot football when he was interviewed for the Newcastle job. He and sporting director Ross Wilson have repeated that promise several times since he was appointed. There has been no sign of it since the opening weekend against Liverpool.

Newcastle are passive, they look disorganised in midfield and weak at the back. Oh and they barely apply pressure let alone attack dangerously.

These are early days but this performance and result had been coming. A pretty brutal reality check after all the positive noise and bold predictions in pre-season. This defeat will drop Newcastle to 12th in the table, where they finished last season under Eddie Howe.

Leeds 4 Newcastle 0 (Okafor) Ampadu hurls it into the box. A defender heads it to the edge of the area where Okafor thumps a left-footed half-volley in off the right post.

Livramento slides in to stop Okafor’s drive down the left, giving Leeds another opportunity to throw it long.

Triple change: Livramento → DedicTouré → Fernandez-PardoWillock → Murphy.

Leeds catch Newcastle playing short from the back. Stach blindsides Steur 20 yards out, tackles him, cuts inside then bends a left foot shot into the side-netting.

After Hall stings Trafford’s palms with a strike from distance. Newcastle want a penalty when the ball hits Tanaka’s arm … but it was outside the area and then Murphy, in frustration, chops down Gudmundsson and takes the booking as an occupational hazard.

Elvedi sloppily gives the ball way to Wissa who tries to set Fernandez-Pardo through down the left. Justin sticks with him and Bogle mops up after Justin was tripped.

He claims he was fouled and wthrashes about like a RL player after he’s tackled. He continues to do a Rumpelstiltskin polka of peevishness towards the ref for a while.

Newcastle corner on the left that Trafford backpedals to tip behind for another.

No changes at half-time for Newcastle as they kick off. Leeds break through the middle promptly and Calvert-Lewin seems to push the ball past Botman and shapes to shoot before Steur slides in with a crucial tackle just inside the box.

The first goal is now an own goal. The explanation is that Tanaka’s shot was on target but the deflection from Steur meant it was going wide until it hit Miley.

Now the second goal has been credited to Bogle as Calvert-Lewin’s header struck the top of his head before it went in.

Sources indicate that you could not say that this scoreline is undeserved. Newcastle are being demolished physically. The central midfield two – Steur and Miley – just don’t have the power to screen their defence.

In a recent development, leeds 3 Newcastle 0 (Calvert-Lewin) Leeds are running all over Newcastle who seem physically flimsy. Calvert-Lewin chops in from the left on to a flick-on, the ball takes a deflection off the Newcastle captain and he steers it into the far corner with a right-foot shot.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9.

Calvert-Lewin is booked for catching Botman in the face with a straight arm rather than a swinging arm. ‘Reckless but not violent.’ Trafford had punchd the corner away at the back post to set Leeds off on a counter.

It has been revealed that tanaka gives the ball away carelessly in midfield and Newcastle work it to Wissa who chops inside past Elvedi, hangs out his own leg looking for contact and hits the deck. The ref waves play on and the ball runs to Barnes in the left of the area. He shapes to shoot but Muharemovic sprinted over to make a fine block-tackle, forcing it behind for a corner.

In a recent development, newcastle are rocking here. They cannot win a tackle.

Industry observers note that for those of us who have watched all Newcastle United’s games this season, this was coming. They do not have any consistent attacking threat, they do no create chances and they are not secure at the back either.

They’ve survived by converting the very few chances they create in games but they have not even had a shot in the first half here.

In a recent development, leeds should be three up after Hornicek fumbled Gudmundsson’s shot from the left. The ball falls to Calvert-Lewin five yards out and he triesto dink it over the keeper who recovers well to smother it.

It has been revealed that leeds 2 Newcastle 0 (Calvert-Lewin) Newcastle try to play the ball out from the back, give it away cheaply to Bogle who feeds Justin haring down the right. He is ostensibly the right centre-back but he is a full-back by trade and stands up a perfect near-post cross that Calvert-Lewin hangs in the air to bury with the firmest of headers. In fact it transpires that his downward header struck Bogle and another deflection benefits rampant Leeds –162 seconds between the goals.

He cushions the pass then lets fly. The ball hits Steur, deflects on to Miley and then loops into the right of the goal with Hornicek understandably stranded.

It has been revealed that ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO.

Good tackle by Steur on Bogle stops the Leeds right-back flying forward after Calvert-Lewin’s flick-on.

Sources indicate that newcastle really are not afraid to launch the ball forward are they? Football tactics are constantly evolving and fashions come back around. What better way to play through a press than to bypass the midfield completely? The hope is it will also cause the centre-backs problems, get them facing their own goal under pressure from one of Newcastle’s rapid forward players in a foot race.

Recent findings suggest that it almost worked a couple of times in the first half but it should be pointed out that the best direct/long ball teams of the past tended to have a striker who was dominant in the air. Newcastle do not presently have one which does limit their threat from flick ons.

Newcastle break from defending a long throw. Wissa carries it 60 yards but with Murphy and Fernadez-Pardo better placed, he tries to shoot from 25 yards and plinks it straight at Trafford, provoking an inevitable ‘Woooooooo’.

According to recent reports, from the resulting long throw Elvedi is found at the back post, unmarked and attempts to volley it towards goal, missing the ball entirely. It was so wild that even the Leeds staff laugh at how inept it was.

Leeds have a corner when they use one of their signature moves, Bogle cutting in from the right across the back four to take a ball over the top. He controls it but cannot force it past Thiaw.

Recent findings suggest that hornicek claws out the corner to Bogle 18 yards out. He puts his laces through a volley that Hornicek parries up high and punches away when he has a second go.

According to recent reports, newcastle chip it long again, this time down the right. Gudmundsson holds off Murphy and Leeds will have the relief of a goal-kick.

Leeds are finding it hard now to play through Newcastle’s high press and the intensity with which they are hounding keeper and defenders.

Newcastle keep looking to use their pace with balls over the top for Wissa, Murphy and Fernandez-Pardo. Wissa closes Trafford down quickly again. He needs to release it with more urgency.

Gonzalez hs not recovered from being struck on the head by the ball and is being replaced by Steur as a concussion sub.

Justin heads over his own bar when Newcastle chip a long pass down the inside right. Wissa beats Muharemovic and tries to find Fernandez-Pardo but Justin got there first. Newcastle go short from the corner and Leeds force them back into their own half.

Sources indicate that terrific save from Hornicek down low to his right. Tanaka’s cross from the left found Justin creeping round the back on the right and heading across goal from the back post. Bogle swivelled and tried a sidewinder flick that was arrowing towards the bottom left corner until the keeper swooped to turn it away with his right hand.

Wissa is ticking, feeling he is getting nothing from the referee when challenging for the ball, the latest incident involving a collision with Justin which was 50-50.

Stach lays it back to Ampadu who hammers a half-volley from 18 yards that poleaxes Calvert-Lewin who was in an offside position.

Sources indicate that newcastle fans sing ‘There’s only one Kevin Keegan’ as the visitors’ defence sweeps the ball around. When they knock the ball up the inisde-right channel Wissa is penalised for swinging his arm and catching Muharemovic in the mooey.

Wissa presses Trafford high and the goalkeeper is a bit too casual but gets away with it. His clearance bounces off the attacker’s shin and loops out to the right. A vicious cross from the left-back hits a Newcastle leg, loops up and smaxks Gonzales flush in the face, knocking him off his feet. The ref stops play.

Industry observers note that two bad moments for Newcastle early on. Lewis Hall caught out by a simple run and pass behind him and then, from the resulting corner Mathias Fernandez-Pardo looked very fortunate, in my opinion, to avoid conceding a penalty for handball.

Recent findings suggest that he got the benefit of the doubt presumably because the ball bounced up onto his hand as he tried to bring it under control and he did not intend to control it with his hand or knock it away. The handball law confuses me but there is a higher threshold now.

Stach tackles Wissa in the centre-circle. Wissa is playing behind Fernandez-Pardo. Ampadu receives a long pass over the top, coming back from an offside position in the nick of time.

Fernandez-Pardo’s outstretched left arm is struck in the penalty area with the ball after they win the header but the ref waves play on and stops the game for a foul on the new striker.

It’s never a problem to come to Elland Road and the singing of Marching On Together before kick-off makes this one of the top three atmospheres in the country, easily. There are problems with VAR, though, and the whole stadium has just seen the ball strike Matias Fernanzes-Pardo’s hand in the area. The reason it is a problem is because we have become conditioned to thinking every time a ball touches someone on the arm in the area, a penalty should be awarded. It is preposterous that faceless beaks have distorted the game so much.

It has been revealed that leeds kick off, attacking the South Stand, from left to right, as they always prefer to do. Justin and Bogle combine on the right and Bogle bends a pass inside HAll to Stach who chooses to cross rather than shoot. It hits Botman and goes out for a corner.

Leeds are in their home kit of white with yellow and blue pinstripe hoops, Newcastle in their navy away kit.

Recent findings suggest that anthony [Elanga] is injured. Unfortunately we have to investigate further how long he will be out but obviously we miss him. We wish him to come back as promptly as possible. It could be [a long-term injury] but he will get another MRI next week and then we’ll see.

Lewis Hall is the perfect player profile for how we play. he is a young lad still and we are very excited [that he has signed a fresh contract].

According to recent reports, the start was not easy. We didn’t have lots of time to prepare for pre-season and that’s one reason we are happy and satisfied with the start. But there is potential and we will work hard on the margins we want to improve.

There will be a lot of excitement surrounding Mathias Fernandez-Pardo’s first start for Newcastle United following his deadline day move from Lille but also keep an eye on Jacob Murphy on the right wing.

Fernandez-Pardo starts with a clean slate at Newcastle, Murphy has a lot of baggage and he has been a popular online target for criticism over the last year or so.

Indeed, some sections of the fanbase were stunned Newcastle rejected a £15m offer from Nottingham Forest on deadline day for a player who has entered the final 12 months of his contract.

Murphy has his limitations, sure and he can be infuriating sometimes when he gives the ball away cheaply, but there is a reason Matthias Jaissle was adamant he could not be sold.

Part of that is due to the fact he does not have another specialist right winger behind Anthony Elanga who misses the Leeds game through injury.

But Murphy is also valued for his experience and his training ground presence. He has been at the club a long time, working under Rafa Benítez, Steve Bruce and Eddie Howe and is a boyhood Newcastle fan.

Jaissle was not willing to lose that from his dressing room. Ultimately, though, Murphy has to perform on the pitch to justify the faith shown in him.

In a recent development, there are not many other options to fill that position while Elanga is missing. Harvey Barnes does not like playing on the right, Amar Dedic is a full back and so is Tino Livramento.

Recent findings suggest that this is an opportunity for Murphy to silence his detractors and prove the faith Jaissle has put in him is not misplaced. At the age of 31, he knows he is not the most popular or appreciated player at the club but he has never shirked or complained about that.

He formed a potent partnership with Alexander Isak when he was leading the line for Newcastle. Can he do the same with the fresh boy Fernandez-Pardo?

Mind you I remember his visit to Elland Road in 1982-83. Not for the faint hearted. In fact it was a disgrace when he was hit by a coin. And yet he was always gracious about Leeds and particularly fond of Don Revie. He was one of very few football people without a strong Leeds United connection who went to his funeral in 1989.

Apparently he was injured in training, the nature of the injury is unspecified.

Newcastle have made a very good start particularly in their transitional moments on the counter-attack. We have to be switched on today to get the next points.

After many years of suffering our supporters deserve it [high expectations]. It’s good but we are far away from not being humble. Our feet are on the ground. We know the second year is always difficult. We have made a good start and it is always vital to ride the momentum as long as possible.

Eddie Howe has left a legacy and the culture he created is still around. Matthias has to work with it. They are unbeaten. they are very dangerous with many pacy players up front. It’s vital not to lose the ball too easily and always be switched on against Newcastle.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Leeds United vs Newcastle United, the last Premier League match of the fourth round of fixtures for the 2026-27 season. Both clubs have made unbeaten starts with one win and two draws each and a win today for wither would send them up to fourth. The two sides met at Elland Road in the third match of last season which ended in a 0-0 draw but the return fixture at St James’ Park was one of the games of the season, a ding-dong match that Leeds led 0-1, 1-2 and 2-3, the latter until the 91st minute and yet still lost 4-3.

In a recent development, the architect of that victory for Newcastle was the Leeds’ fans’ incubus, a player commonly known around Elland Road as ‘Harvey F------- Barnes’. His two goals that night were his sixth and seventh against Leeds in eight matches for Leicester and the Toon. Back in the last century and at the turn of this one, Alan Shearer scored 21 league goals in 23 games against Leeds for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle, it can feel like one bogeyman passing the baton to another.

Newcastle’s sound form with their new model team this season has been based on searing pace and their ability on the counter whether with runners, in the case of Anthony Elanga, or with long diagonals against Tottenham that ripped a hole in the left side of their defence. Leeds rallied from being overrun by Brentford at half-time in their last home game to switch from three at the back to four and wrest back the initiative and while they reverted for the Brighton draw, in both games it was the introduction of Ao Tanaka in midfield that gave them control.

Industry observers note that it is genuinely hard to decide whether the 6-3 defeat by Chelsea in the Carabao Cup from being 2-0 up at Stamford Bridge is significant to Leeds league form. One simplistic way of looking at it would be to say Leeds reserves were better than Chelsea’s reserves in the first half and Chelsea’s first-team were better than Leeds reserves and their shaky, debutant keeper in the second. But any similar defensive frailties tonight and there will be jitters over the next week before the international break. Newcastle, by contrast, toiled in their 1-0 victory over Millwall but the result glosses over a lack of incision for long spells of it.

Breaking: Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala's camp issue joint statement after contract pressure controversy

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 18:40.
  • Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala's representatives have issued a joint statement following talks aimed at easing tensions over the midfielder's health and contract, just days after the club was accused of putting public pressure on the Germany international.
  • The 23-year-old's future has become a sensitive subject at the Allianz Arena, with senior Bayern figures openly questioning whether he can regain his previous level following a difficult period of medical problems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 18:40.

Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala's representatives have issued a joint statement following talks aimed at easing tensions over the midfielder's health and contract, just days after the club was accused of putting public pressure on the Germany international.

The 23-year-old's future has become a sensitive subject at the Allianz Arena, with senior Bayern figures openly questioning whether he can regain his previous level following a difficult period of medical problems.

Those remarks prompted criticism from global players' union FIFPRO, which accused the German champions of pursuing a "coordinated strategy" to pressure Musiala and his representatives ahead of possible contract discussions.

Sources indicate that however, Bayern have now taken a significant step towards addressing the controversy. Following a meeting on Tuesday, November 24, the club and Musiala's agency, 11WINS, published a statement emphasising their shared commitment to the player's recovery and clarifying an important detail about his medical history.

The announcement comes less than a week after Musiala returned to action during Bayern's 1-1 Bundesliga draw with Cologne, having missed almost two months through injury.

In a statement published on their official website on Wednesday, Bayern confirmed that discussions with Musiala's management had taken place the previous day.

"A constructive meeting took place between FC Bayern Munich and the management of Jamal Musiala yesterday (Tuesday)," the club revealed.

"For both sides, the player's health comes above everything else. Musiala is being given full support on his road back.".

The statement also addressed speculation surrounding the timing of the midfielder's neurological symptoms, which became public earlier this year.

Bayern and 11WINS confirmed that Musiala underwent his first examination for absence-like symptoms on April 22, 2025, immediately after they initially appeared.

Crucially, that examination took place more than two months after the Germany international signed his contract extension until June 2030 on February 14, 2025.

The clarification establishes that the medical concerns arose after the agreement was completed, addressing speculation about whether the condition had been known when the lucrative deal was negotiated.

Bayern added that the examination had been conducted in consultation with the club and its medical department.

The statement concluded by confirming that the two parties had agreed to maintain contact and continue discussions "in a spirit of partnership and trust".

According to Sky Germany, Musiala's representatives Christian Schmid and Tobias Altschaffl attended Tuesday's meeting with Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen, president Herbert Hainer and sporting director Max Eberl.

Notably, honorary president Uli Hoeness and supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, whose earlier comments contributed to the controversy, were not present.

The joint statement represents a change in tone following several weeks of increasingly public discussion about Musiala's situation.

Hoeness, Dreesen and Rummenigge had all raised questions about the potential consequences if the attacking midfielder failed to recover his previous form.

Rummenigge was particularly outspoken after Friday's draw with Cologne, suggesting that Bayern might eventually have to reconsider the financial terms of Musiala's contract if his performances did not justify the sums involved.

Those comments attracted criticism from FIFPRO, which argued that the club's senior figures were placing unnecessary pressure on a player dealing with significant health concerns.

The union called for contractual matters to be handled privately and emphasised the importance of respecting agreements already signed by both parties.

Further questions emerged following a report by Suddeutsche Zeitung about a meeting between Hoeness and Musiala's agent during the summer.

According to the German newspaper, Hoeness believed there had been a verbal understanding that the midfielder's contract could be revisited if his condition prevented him from returning to his former level.

Musiala's representatives reportedly interpreted that discussion differently, understanding only that the parties could hold further talks if the player's situation failed to improve.

Tuesday's meeting did not produce any announced agreement to alter the contract.

Indeed, Eberl told Sky Germany that salary matters had not been discussed, with the immediate focus instead placed on supporting Musiala's return.

The sporting director also expressed confidence that the midfielder could regain his best form, stressing the need to give him time without additional pressure.

Musiala's contract remains valid until 2030, and neither Bayern nor his representatives have announced any changes to its terms.

The joint statement therefore provides an key clarification about the circumstances surrounding the original agreement, while leaving the longer-term contractual questions unresolved.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Vincent Kompany did not delve too deep into Bayern Munich's defeat to Lille in the Champions League, instead urging his players to embrace the fight of reaching the knockouts.

Bayern were beaten for the first time in Europe this season at the Stade Pierre-Mauroy on Wednesday, with Aleksandar Pavlovic's own goal sealing a 2-1 victory for Lille.

Despite having both Harry Kane and Michael Olise out injured, Kompany's side took the lead in the 15th minute when Dayot Upamecano nodded in from Tom Bischof's corner.

However, Lille turned the game on its head in the space of three second-half minutes, with Ayase Ueda curling into the bottom corner after seeing an earlier goal ruled out for a foul on Joshua Kimmich, with his strike chalked off after a VAR review.

And Lille profited from some misfortune in the 65th minute. Ethan Mbappe's shot hit the right post, with Pavlovic comically turning into his own net under no real pressure.

The result saw Bayern lose a Champions League group stage game having been ahead at half-time for the first time since November 2014 against Manchester City (3-2).

Bayern were also beaten by a French side other than Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League for the first time since November 2009 (2-0 against Bordeaux), having won seven in a row in between against Lyon (three), Marseille and Lille (both two).

Kompany's side are now 15th in the 36-team standings and two points adrift of the top eight, with fixtures against Slavia Prague, Manchester United and Real Betis remaining.

Industry observers note that "We tried, so I can't blame the energy. The second goal obviously shouldn't happen," Kompany told reporters.

"But like I said, I know these moments from my experience. We now have to fight for our own luck. Stick together, battle and also enjoy this fight a bit.".

Bayern largely kept Lille at bay in the first half, with Ueda drawing a fine stop from Jonas Urbig – in for the injured Manuel Neuer – soon after Upamecano's opener.

Hiroki Ito flicked a header wide and Mbappe saw another chance saved, while Berke Ozer had to be on his toes to keep Konrad Laimer out at the other end.

In a recent development, "The first half was exactly how we imagined, in terms of our strengths and also our weaknesses," Kompany added. "But overall it was a very good first half.

In a recent development, "Then we just didn't get into our rhythm any more in the second half. That's part of football, you always have to play your game until the last minute.".

There were just 213 seconds between Ueda's equaliser for Lille in the 62nd minute and Pavlovic's own goal in the 65th minute to put the French team ahead.

Lille's dominance in the second half was backed up by the statistics, with their expected goals (xG) total of 1.49 from their 10 attempts dwarfing Bayern's tally of 0.22 from their six shots, with only two of those on target.

"We played a very decent first half, where we implemented a lot of things in the way we wanted. We were aggressive and had good energy," Laimer said.

It has been revealed that "We lost that a bit in the second half. Then we concede the two goals, which happened too easily. We no longer produced what we're capable of.

"If you don't reach your highest possible level in the Champions League, you'll come away with nothing.

It has been revealed that "We stick together and try, with the players we have, to play our football. Now it's about recovering promptly because it continues already on Saturday.".

The France international was initially named in the Europa League squad despite undergoing foot surgery in the summer.

However, Kroupi’s absence allowed Bournemouth to use UEFA’s temporary injury replacement rule to include Ben Gannon-Doak for the first four games in the league phase.

Kroupi returned to action last month, but as a result of Gannon-Doak’s inclusion in the Europa League squad, he was unable to feature in the 3-1 win over Sparta Prague at the start of the month.

Industry observers note that "Everyone is ready,” Rose said. "We have no fresh injuries ahead of tomorrow's game.

“We are glad to have Alex and Junior back and available.".

When asked whether the pair will start in Vigo, Rose said: "It could be possible, but also maybe not. We will see".

In regard to absentees, the Cherries are without the injured trio of Julian Araujo, Juanlu Sanchez and Alex Toth.

Bournemouth are presently enjoying the longest winning run in the club's history after recording a ninth consecutive victory in all competitions at the weekend.

They also boast a perfect record in their maiden European campaign, having won their four league phase matches by a combined 11-2 scoreline.

As a result, they head into matchday five in second spot in the Europa League league phase and five points clear of the teams sitting just outside the top eight.

Published: 09:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 12:29 EST, 24 November 2026.

They had a World Cup winner in defence, Superman in their squad and a Sex Pistol in charge of recruitment.

There's a clue in the name, but Hollywood United must have been the wildest, most star-studded pub football team of all time.

Ray Winstone, Jason Statham, Mike Myers and Vinnie Jones all turned out for a team that grew out of a gathering of British expats at the Cat & Fiddle pub in the late Eighties.

It being Hollywood, they travelled to matches by private jet and they even took on David Beckham in a charity match.

Now, as the Sex Pistols prepare to embark on a tour marking the 50th anniversary of their debut single, guitarist Steve Jones has revealed how he assembled the extraordinary side on Hollywood's Sunset Boulevard.

Among those who pulled on the shirt were France's World Cup-winning defender Frank Leboeuf, former Scotland captain Richard Gough and Brandon Routh, the American actor who played the superhero in the 2006 film Superman Returns.

Routh was given no special treatment by his team-mates, who would mockingly shout ‘Superman!’ whenever he made a mistake.

Hollywood United is the world's most famous pub team - featuring a littany of high-profile stars.

Created by British expat and Sex Pistols star Steve Jones (right), United have rubbed shoulders with the likes of David Beckham.

Vinnie Jones, meanwhile, had apparently lost none of the competitive instincts that characterised his career in English football.

In 2002, it was reported that he had been sent off just 15 seconds after coming on as a substitute in a Hollywood United friendly.

Anthony LaPaglia, the Australian actor who starred in the hit television series Without a Trace, was their goalkeeper.

There were members of the Sex Pistols, The Cult and Def Leppard, as well as actors such as Ralf Little.

But there were also rather less celebrated footballers.

‘The start of it was with me and Anthony LaPaglia; he was a goalie, and from there it turned into Hollywood United,’ Jones told the Telegraph.

‘We always used to play in a league with a bunch of regular blokes, carpenters and so on, then we got a few more faces who wanted to start kicking about with us like Vinnie Jones.’.

The two Joneses met in a video shop in Los Angeles and the former Wimbledon hardman, who had embarked on a film career with Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels, needed little persuasion to join.

Sources indicate that ‘He was up for a laugh, and he knows where to put a ball. Most of the team were amateurs, but we were decent and reached a certain level.’.

In November 2007, Hollywood United took on Beckham's LA Galaxy in a charity match.

Sources indicate that england manager Steve McClaren had flown to California to assess Beckham's fitness ahead of a European Championship qualifier against Croatia. It's not clear whether he attended the match, which Hollywood United lost 12-4. Beckham scored twice, as did Leboeuf and over 5,000 spectators raised more than $100,000 for victims of the California wildfires.

Steve Jones, now 71, had himself broken one of football's golden rules by changing his allegiance.

Vinnie Jones (left) and Ray Winstone (right) have turned out for the amateur football team.

Actor Anthony LaPaglia lets the team travel on his private jet to matches across America.

Having followed QPR as a schoolboy in west London and also been associated with Fulham, he became a Chelsea supporter after moving to California and getting sober.

Chelsea's games were available on American television and his lifelong friend and fellow Sex Pistol Paul Cook was already a diehard Blues fan.

Hollywood United played at Griffith Park, beneath the famous Hollywood sign, but their adventures would take them considerably further afield.

LaPaglia would arrange private jets to transport the players to matches.

Gough recalls one trip when the team flew to Vancouver for a charity match before heading straight to the Mexican resort of Puerto Vallarta to play a side of former Mexico internationals.

Vinnie Jones also told the Guardian in 2007 that Hollywood United had fielded nine former international footballers in a single match.

The club's ranks included former Liverpool and Newcastle defender Barry Venison and United States internationals Alexi Lalas and Eric Wynalda.

Winstone, a lifelong West Ham fan, found playing in the Californian heat rather more demanding than he had anticipated.

He later recalled being so exhausted by the time the ball reached him that he was barely able to kick it. And he wasn't particularly impressed by the willingness of former Chelsea defender Leboeuf to pass the ball, describing the Frenchman as a greedy player.

Among those watching from the touchline was the actor John Hurt, who was in town filming Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull with Winstone.

Some of the rock stars had impressive footballing pedigrees.

Ian Astbury, the lead singer of The Cult, had played boys' club football in Glasgow alongside future Everton and Scotland striker Graeme Sharp.

Gough, meanwhile, struck up a conversation with a team-mate from Northern Ireland without having the slightest idea he was Vivian Campbell, the guitarist of Def Leppard.

Sex Pistol Jones, who has lived in Los Angeles for more than 40 years, is returning to Britain next month for a tour marking the 50th anniversary of the release of Anarchy in the UK.

He still regularly attends football matches whenever he is back in England, although he has little time for the corporate hospitality enjoyed by many of his celebrity contemporaries.

‘I don't care where I sit, but I'm not interested in sitting in some box with a bunch of t***ers.’.

#198043. From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated

From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated

📅 26 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1049 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes.
  • But as Americans vote in the US midterm elections, it's time to think about how disgust shapes our politics, or whether our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?
  • The smell of rotten food can make us recoil.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes.

But as Americans vote in the US midterm elections, it's time to think about how disgust shapes our politics, or whether our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

The smell of rotten food can make us recoil. Certain sexual practices can provoke a similar reaction. And in today's polarized political climate, even political opponents can become objects of disgust.

Psychologists have long investigated whether sensitivity to disgust helps explain political beliefs. A review of 24 studies found that people who reported being more easily disgusted tended to hold more socially conservative views.

One explanation begins with evolution.

"We think that it evolved in part to reduce exposure to things that could make you sick," psychologist Yoel Inbar, of the University of British Columbia in Canada, told DW.

According to recent reports, but disgust is not a single emotion. The Three-Domain Disgust Scale, developed in 2009, distinguishes three types:.

One theory is that people who are especially wary of germs and disease may also prefer traditional social rules.

Inbar explains that avoiding potential sources of infection can also mean missing out on fresh experiences.

"Some people are more on the cautious conservative side, and some people are more on the exploring risk-taking side when it comes to pathogen exposure," he stated.

Indeed, the language of contamination also appears in political rhetoric. During his 2024 presidential campaign, Donald Trump repeatedly described immigrants as "poisoning the blood of our country." Trump has also described himself as a "germaphobe.".

Inbar acknowledges that the evidence linking sensitivity to disgust with conservative political beliefs remains uncertain.

It has been revealed that "We have hypotheses. I don't know that we have as strong of evidence as I would like," Inbar stated.

According to recent reports, disgust is not exclusively conservative. And what people find revolting can depend on their values.

A 2020 study titled "Is Disgust a "Conservative" Emotion?" found that liberals and conservatives were disgusted by different things.

Conservatives, generally aligned with the Republicans in US politics, reported greater disgust at examples involving sexual behaviors and drug use, while liberals, generally aligned with the Democrats, reported greater disgust at animal abuse and environmental pollution.

However, when asked how easily disgusted they were in general, there was no clear difference across the political spectrum.

Some early studies suggested conservatives revealed stronger physical reactions to frightening or disgusting images, measured partly through changes in sweating.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

But subsequent research, including a 2020 study by political psychologist Bert Bakker at the University of Amsterdam, struggled to reproduce those findings.

Studies based on questionnaires, however, have generally found that people with more conservative attitudes report being more easily disgusted.

"If bodily reactions don't differ across political groups, why do feelings?" Manos Tsakiris, of Royal Holloway and the Centre for the Politics of Feelings at the University of London, told DW.

Tsakiris and colleague Mariana von Mohr wondered whether the answer might lie in how people perceive and interpret signals from their bodies.

Scientists call the perception of internal sensations, such as hunger, breathing or a racing heart, "interoception." It's sometimes called our eighth sense, alongside the familiar five, plus our senses of balance and body position.

"A bodily signal doesn't arrive with a label attached," Tsakiris told DW. "We have to notice it and make sense of it.".

The researchers surveyed 632 US adults, asking how much they noticed and trusted signals from their bodies — a measure known as "interoceptive sensibility.".

They found that people who were more easily disgusted by sexual behavior tended to be more conservative, regardless of how aware they felt of their bodies.

But for moral disgust, the link to conservatism was found only among people who reported lower bodily awareness.

What particularly surprised Tsakiris was that perceived bodily awareness alone had no link to political views.

"People who are highly attuned to their bodies were neither more liberal nor more conservative," he said.

Inbar questions whether all forms of disgust are equally useful for studying political attitudes.

He and Joshua Tybur, one of the creators of the Three-Domain Disgust Scale, generally prefer measuring pathogen disgust — reactions to potential sources of disease — rather than sexual disgust.

Questions about sexual disgust may already reflect conservative beliefs about sex.

"It's almost asking people the same thing twice," Inbar stated.

The latest study found no significant link between pathogen disgust and conservative views.

In a recent development, inbar wants the findings on bodily awareness and disgust tested again, with predictions set out in advance. For now, he considers them "suggestive at best.".

Tsakiris suggests that people who struggle to understand their bodily feelings may be more vulnerable to political messages telling them what those feelings mean.

"I know what you're feeling. You're feeling angry or you're feeling disgusted about this thing," he remarked, illustrating how someone might put an emotional label on another person's unease.

Such labels could influence political behavior, he argues, although the study did not directly test this.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"This is how disgust can do political work: it can turn moral judgments about individuals into judgments about whole groups," he remarked.

The research cannot establish whether disgust shapes political beliefs or existing beliefs shape what people find disgusting. Bakker notes that political beliefs can influence how people describe their own personalities, suggesting the relationship could work both ways.

"Voting behavior is very complex and citizens make up their mind about politics in a complex way," he told DW.

According to recent reports, inbar also cautions against exaggerating disgust's importance. "The thing to emphasize in your story is that the relationship, while it's consistent, is quite small," he noted.

"It's one of the many influences on people's politics.".

Tsakiris advocates what he calls "critical feeling": questioning our emotional responses to provocative material, including social media posts, just as we question the information itself.

He also emphasizes discussing our feelings with others and listening to different perspectives, even when we disagree.

"Life and politics and democracy is a contact sport," he said. Edited by: Rosalie Delaney.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri.

Sources indicate that I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice.

A quick glance at two contrasting stats sums up exactly where Arsenal’s shortcomings lie at the moment.

Sources indicate that mikel Arteta’s side are still in fine shape to progress straight through to the last 16 as one of the top-eight sides in the Champions League. Only the Gunners, holders Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid remain unbeaten in this season’s competition.

According to recent reports, however, it could have been so much better, after an extraordinarily wasteful display in the draw with Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night. Arsenal registered 30 shots, but only four on target and they scored just once.

It should have been so much more for Martin Odegaard, too. He has registered only one assist in Europe this season, ranking him 45th in the competition for that metric.

And yet for expected assists, per FotMob, Odegaard ranks top across the entire Champions League. Above Nico Paz, who has five assists to his name, and Lamine Yamal, who has three.

Arsenal have had no glitch creating chances. Against Dortmund, Odegaard laid on nine of them, the most by any player in a Champions League match this season.

That was just the second time this decade that an Arsenal player has created more than five chances in a Champions League match. The other example? Odegaard against Napoli in September.

In a recent development, the discourse around Odegaard is often hypercritical. That, to an extent, is understandable. He has been the captain and creative heartbeat of the team in a period in which, for all it has been successful, there have been ongoing questions surrounding the attack.

It is perhaps also a hangover from the last two seasons, when injuries hampered Odegaard and he was well off his best. Frustration towards him built and some minds appear to have been made up.

However, the criticism that he does not deliver consistently enough just does not hold up to scrutiny this season.

Man City get appeal verdict revision ahead of Arsenal clash.

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal told Kroupi decision; Liverpool done deal.

Tottenham beat Arsenal to exciting transfer coup as signing confirmed.

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway.

From the moment Odegaard returned to the club in the summer after a strong World Cup with Norway, he has looked back to his best. That started with his sublime goal against Manchester City in the Community Shield and has continued since.

For all there have been some notable exceptions, Arsenal have on the whole played much better football this season. They have been far more free-flowing and fluid in attack.

In a recent development, odegaard has been central to that. Along with his chance creation stats in Europe, Odegaard is also second for expected assists in the Premier League.

He is taking more responsibility in front of goal, too. Odegaard is Arsenal’s top scorer this season and is only one league goal shy of his combined tally from the last two seasons.

If there has been a dip in Arsenal’s attack from the start of this season, that is not down to Odegaard. Bukayo Saka, who was displaying far better goalscoring instincts, suffering a quad injury, and Kai Havertz’s performance levels dropping significantly are far more relevant explanations.

Arsenal do have a problem in attack - but it is not Odegaard.

Odegaard has been the most consistent forward player. It is not just the chances created or even the goals, but his influence in all facets of Arsenal’s game as almost an extension of Arteta on the pitch. He is the leader of the press, and that led to the winning goal against Liverpool at Anfield earlier this month.

Arsenal do have a problem in attack - but it is not Odegaard. It is not an exaggeration to say that Viktor Gyokeres should have scored another three goals against Dortmund from chances created by Odegaard alone.

The Gunners are not clinical enough but that is not the fault of the player creating the chances. Nor is it a coaching concern. Arteta could not have done more to deliver a win against Dortmund.

The problem is a personnel one. The quality of Arsenal’s attackers does not come close to matching the level in every other position in the squad. At least one top-class winger signing is required, along with a new striker.

It was clear at the end of last season that significant upgrades were needed. Instead, Arsenal sold three forwards and signed only Christos Tzolis.

Sources indicate that that is the substantial failure and where the fingers should be pointing. Not at Odegaard for occasionally taking too many touches or making a wrong decision on the counter.

Odegaard’s contract situation adds another factor to the debate over his role in the team. He is nearing the final 18 months of his current deal.

Talks have not yet begun over an extension, Odegaard revealed during the international break, but that should be a no-brainer for Arsenal.

That will require the club to make another significant financial commitment, following on from several other upcoming contracts for key players, but it is still a far cheaper alternative to trying to sign a replacement of Odegaard’s quality.

Securing Odegaard’s future should be the club’s next top priority, swiftly followed by then delivering him the forwards he deserves.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Luis Enrique insisted Paris Saint-Germain's 2-2 draw with Roma in the Champions League on Wednesday was their "hardest match of the season so far".

PSG dropped points for the first time in Europe this season, with the stalemate ending their run of 12 consecutive victories in the competition in the process.

Mario Hermoso's fifth-minute goal was cancelled out by Illia Zabarnyi's header in the first half at the Parc des Princes, with the hosts getting themselves in front just after the hour.

Achraf Hakimi was brought down by Wesley inside the penalty area with Ousmane Dembele scoring from 12 yards out, but Roma were awarded a spot-kick of their own late on.

Vitinha was penalised for a handball and Donyell Malen stepped up to seal a share of the spoils, though Roma may count themselves unlucky, given they finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 2.65 from their 13 shots to PSG's tally of 1.73 from their 15 attempts.

Indeed, PSG managed just four shots on target against Roma, their fewest in a Champions League group stage match since November 2024 against Bayern Munich (three).

PSG were, of course, without long-term absentees Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, though Luis Enrique acknowledged there were problems elsewhere in his team.

Recent findings suggest that "We knew before the match that it was going to be tough. Right from the first few minutes, they pressed us relentlessly, and it was very difficult," Luis Enrique said.

"We had problems right from the start of the game, and we could even have lost this one. They deserved a draw, perhaps even a win.

"It was very tough; I think it's been the hardest match of the season so far. That's how tough this competition is. There are good games and tough games.

"We need to be aware of that, accept it and stay on our toes, because it's a very tough competition. We've still got three matches left in this group stage.

"We need to prepare and get the players back that are working their way back to full fitness.".

All square between Paris and Rome. https://t.co/XSOyzRwPsx https://t.co/rntl4bQY0u.

— Paris Saint-Germain (@PSG_English) November 26, 2026.

Roma are one of four teams to go 1-0 ahead in all five of their Champions League games this season, alongside Arsenal, Como and Galatasaray.

They have, however, failed to win four of those (D2 L2), the most games failed to win in a group campaign after scoring first since Atalanta in 2021-22 (also four).

It was a result that also saw PSG concede first, later lead, but failed to win a Champions League group stage game at home for the first time in the competition.

There were positives, though. Only PSG themselves in 2017-18 (24) have scored more goals across their opening five games of a Champions League campaign than Luis Enrique's side in 2026-27 (22).

In a recent development, "It was a difficult match. They were strong defensively, and it was a bit of a challenge for us, particularly in the penalty box," Luis Enrique added. "It was a very, very tough match.

In a recent development, "They'd analysed our team well and I think that made a difference. We tried to play our own game, to keep possession from start to finish, but we didn't manage it.

Industry observers note that "We dropped two points, but we didn't lose, and that's very crucial. I think it's good for the squad; we're staying strong, and now we're already focusing on the next match.".

Dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

Arsenal have won the League Cup twice – in 1987 and 1993 – meaning eight clubs have better records, including Aston Villa (five titles), Tottenham Hotspur (four), Nottingham Forest (four) and Leicester City (three).

It has been revealed that their rather modest haul is a far cry from their record-setting 14 FA Cup titles. In the 33-years since Arsenal’s most recent League Cup triumph, the competition’s title sponsor has changed hands four times (kudos to anyone who can name all five!).

But I have faith in them, it’s just that everyone’s fit at the moment and we’ve had to recruit a strong squad to get us through an unbelievably challenging season.

“On Tuesday, whoever I pick, I have 100 per cent faith that they’re ready and that they’re going to represent what we do and how we go about it.”.

“Some players were carrying some fatigue, some little issues that we have to look after and some other players are available, fresh and in better conditions to play.

Alan Davies, the actor and comedian who is a famously passionate supporter of Arsenal, recently told a story about a charity event he once attended with former captain Tony Adams. Speaking on The Tuesday Club podcast, Davies stated Adams revealed his football philosophy to be: “You need seven.”.

Sources indicate that the “seven” in question, Adams explained, are seven members of the team who are ready and willing to fight the opposition in the tunnel after the game. Once a team have those seven individuals, Adams said, everything else flows from there.

It has been revealed that for much of the past two decades, Arsenal have not had seven. In some years in the latter stages of Arsène Wenger’s tenure, they probably did not even have three or four. But that has all changed in recent seasons under Mikel Arteta, to such an extent that the Premier League champions would now undoubtedly bring considerably more than seven combatants to any touchline scrap or tunnel bust-up.

Saturday’s gritty 2-0 victory away to Sunderland provided evidence that Arsenal have added two more of these characters to their squad this summer.

Although keeping Ipswich in the Premier League must be Gary O’Neil’s primary goal, he has insisted that the club will embrace opportunities in the cups.

When asked how he would approach tonight’s tie, O’Neil stated: “We’ll have a strong side, we’ve worked our socks off in the transfer window to give ourselves a strong squad. Of course, a different level to Arsenal, but we’ll be strong on Tuesday and we’ll do our best to win the game.

“The club has worked so hard to have these moments and of course it’s a cup game, but to have Arsenal and Liverpool come to Portman Road a week or so apart is what everyone has worked so hard for in recent years, so we’re going to enjoy it, we’re going to have a right go and worst thing that can happen is we lose to Arsenal.”.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of the Carabao Cup third-round tie between Ipswich Town and Arsenal. Mikel Arteta’s side have won all six of their matches so far this season, but travel to Portman Road fresh off an incident-filled win over Sunderland which thrust officiating back into the spotlight after Ezri Konsa conceded a penalty having been – in Arteta’s words – “judo-rolled” by Dan Ballard.

According to recent reports, after the match, the Arsenal manager said: “I watched [the incident] 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how to even think to give a penalty in this situation or the way the VAR has to intervene. So I don’t know what to think, really. But I’m sad, that we have to discuss, after such a beautiful game, something at this level that has the gravity of that because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship… This cannot happen.”.

Arteta may be pleased that VAR is not in use at this stage of the Carabao Cup, and all eyes will be on Peter Bankes who takes charge of tonight’s match against Ipswich.

This season Arsenal hope to arrest a startling League Cup record. It has been 33 years since they last lifted the trophy, during which time they have been runners-up seven times. Losing last year’s final will have also added fuel to Arsenal’s fire, and Arteta may resolve he must field a strong starting XI. In fact, he may not have much choice in his backline as Ben White has emerged as a serious injury doubt after picking up an injury at the Stadium of Light and may join Cristhian Mosquera and William Saliba on the treatment table. This would likely mean starting Jurriën Timber, who is only just returning from a long-term groin issue. There is more scope for rotation in advanced positions, with Noni Madueke, Viktor Gyokeres, Eberechi Eze and Mikel Merino contenders to start.

A 90th-minute Zian Flemming winner against Crystal Palace on Saturday helped Gary O’Neil’s Ipswich to their second win in four Premier League games, a feat they required 16 matches to achieve the last time they were in the top flight. Heavy investment into Ipswich’s squad has proved fruitful thus far, though in-form striker Emersonn is expected to sit out tonight having taken a knock at Selhurst Park.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Francesco Camarda has spoken about his Champions League goal that never was today, and how it was an AC Milan dream come true.

Camarda first became known to Milan as a youngster, but he revealed himself further when he became Serie A’s youngest-ever appearance maker. He almost then went to a European level, with a goal in the Champions League. However, it wasn’t to be.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

According to recent reports, on his debut in the competition, the starlet bagged a goal which would’ve made him the Rossoneri’s youngest-ever scorer in Europe’s main stage. Yet it was ruled out for offside and a few years on, the now 18-year-old is still waiting for a first competitive goal for the Diavolo.

Speaking to Vice, the striker opened up about his dream of playing in the Champions League at San Siro, his emotions after his goal (and it later being disallowed) and how his teammates rallied around him, as MilanVibes relayed.

“As a child, I used to say to my dad: imagine if one day I could walk into San Siro and hear the Champions League anthem, accompanied by the roar of the entire stadium. When it actually happened, I thought back to that little boy and realised I had realised a dream.

Sources indicate that “When I stepped onto the pitch, I had an incredible adrenaline rush. Then the goal came, and I felt the whole stadium explode. I also felt the affection of my teammates, who immediately raised me into the air.

“However, when I looked at the scoreboard and saw that the VAR check was in progress, I was already convinced the goal would be disallowed.

“When I returned home that evening, with my parents and cousin, I burst into tears. I was overjoyed by the goal, but at the same time deeply disappointed by what had happened. It wasn’t easy at first, but I also worked on my mental health and managed to put that moment behind me.

“Today, I’m proud of the journey I’ve taken and of having overcome those difficulties.”.

Recent findings suggest that “I remember what Gabbia told me: he was sorry for what happened, but he explained that the experience should give me even more motivation. It should push me to improve, to train harder, and to work so I can relive even more wonderful emotions.”.

“In football, there are positive and negative opinions; it has always been this way and will continue to be this way. A player’s true strength lies in not being influenced by what is said, because, regardless of whether you do well or badly, someone will always find a reason to judge you.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 25 Nov 2026 19:55, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 19:57.

Anthony Gordon created Champions League history in Barcelona's 4-1 success over Sabah in the league stage of the competition on Wednesday night.

The England international scored twice in Azerbaijan to play a leading role in Hansi Flick's side securing an impressive win in the European Cup.

Gordon has now scored six Champions League goals in Azerbaijan, which is the most any English player has netted in away games in one country in the tournament.

Four of the attacker's goals in Azerbaijan came against Qarabag during his time with Newcastle United, before scoring twice more against Sabah.

Recent findings suggest that 6 - Anthony Gordon's six UEFA Champions League goals in Azerbaijan are the most any English player has scored in away games in one country in the competition. Tourist. https://t.co/7OfdYkdzch.

The 25-year-old is now on five goals and five assists in 17 appearances for Barcelona since his arrival at the club from Newcastle.

Meanwhile, Gordon's overall record in the Champions League is 13 goals and two assists in 23 appearances in the tournament.

Barcelona have now picked up 12 points from their five matches in the league stage of the Champions League, which has left them in fourth spot in the overall table.

Flick's team were missing Lamine Yamal on Wednesday due to a slight ankle injury; in his absence, Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus were also on the scoresheet.

Barcelona will be aiming to make it six straight wins in all competitions when they continue their La Liga campaign against Deportivo La Coruna on Sunday afternoon.

The Catalan outfit will then welcome Atletico Madrid to Camp Nou in their first match of December, before facing Celta Vigo in their third league game in quick succession.

Barcelona's next Champions League game is at home to Manchester City on December 8.

Latest Update: Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Janosch, the pen name of German author and illustrator Horst Eckert, won hearts around the world with his warm and simple sense of humor. He charmed children and adults alike with his iconic Tiger, Bear, Tiger-Duck and other animals.

Janosch created more than 150 books, which have been translated into over 30 languages.

Sources indicate that his best-selling children's book, "Oh, wie schön ist Panama," translated into English as "The Trip to Panama," was so lucrative that Janosch was able to settle down on the Canary Island of Tenerife in 1980, where he lived together with his wife Ines. The writer and illustrator died peacefully at the age of 95, his publisher Bernhard Feil announced on Wednesday.

Janosch was born as Horst Eckert on March 11, 1931, in Hindenburg (now Zabrze, Poland) in what was then Upper Silesia. After World War II, his family had to flee to Germany.

Industry observers note that in 1953, Janosch started studying at the Academy of Art in Munich, thinking that it would be easy to become an artist. He was however dismissed after just a few terms for "lack of talent.".

It has been revealed that but luckily for his later readers, Janosch did not give up. He continued to work as a freelance artist, soon discovering his second great gift, namely writing.

His first children's book about a horse named Valek was published in 1960.

Although Janosch became famous primarily for his children's books, he also wrote books for adults that focused on his own childhood.

In a recent development, even though he wrote cheerful books for children, Janosch hardly had any positive memories of his own childhood, as his father was an alcoholic. He was beaten not only by him but also by his mother and grandmother. Raised in a strictly Catholic environment, he was continuously threatened to be punished by God.

Later on, Janosch tried to overcome the burden of his childhood memories by turning to alcohol as well.

He always expressed a great deal of understanding for children, trying to encourage them to stand up for their rights. As a result of his childhood experiences, Janosch did not want to have children himself, and his attitude towards the Catholic Church always remained divided. "As I am a sinner and a heretic, God will let me live a long life so that I can return to the Church," he told his biographer Angela Bajorek.

It has been revealed that janosch's animal figures are endearing but not always well-behaved. They love all kinds of nonsense. But even if they lie to each other or put their own interests first, the true winner at the end of stories is always friendship and solidarity.

In a recent development, janosch achieved his major breakthrough with "The Trip to Panama," a story about two friends, a little tiger and a bear, who set out to find their paradise in Panama. After touring around in circles, they finally end up where they started out; they realize that their journey was the destination. Janosch received the German Youth Book Prize in 1979 for the work.

Recent findings suggest that janosch's protagonists have become familiar to generations of children all over the world. They come up over and over again in the various stories carefully illustrated with water colors.

There is the honest lion Hans from the toy chest who fails to catch a nutcracker with his lies. There is Schnuddel and a ridiculous bragger Günter the Box-Frog. And then there is a tiger that collects mushrooms while looking out for his devoted friend, a bear, who always stands up for him even when the tiger temporarily leaves him because of a little pig in one of the stories.

The "Tigerente," literally "Tiger-Duck," a wooden duck on wheels with yellow-brown stripes, appears on numerous pictures by the illustrator. At times, the animal has been tossed into a corner, at times it is hanging from the ceiling, or the Box-Frog pulls it across the drawing.

His iconic figures, especially the Tiger-Duck, have served as motifs on various items, from cups to stamps to jewelry, and even on airplanes. Film adaptations and TV series based on his stories were produced in German and English.

Guests who visited Janosch in Tenerife were impressed by his very modest lifestyle. He always said that hanging around in his hammock doing nothing was what he enjoyed most. And yet Janosch remained very active until the end of his life.

Sources indicate that from 2013 to 2019, he wrote a column for the German weekly Die Zeit, taking on the role of Mr. Wondrak, who commented on world affairs. Shortly before his 90th birthday in 2021, the complete collection of his Mr. Wondrak columns were published as a book in German.

Like the protagonists in his stories, Janosch always tried to content himself with few things. As he wrote in one of his books: "He who needs almost nothing, has everything.".

This article was originally written in German.
