Industry observers note that A total of 11 VUS/CCOP variants (AAC ≥ 10) had absolute effect sizes exceeding 7.99 cm, with P values ranging from 1.6 × 10−4 to 1.1 × 10−31 (five with P < 1.75 × 10−9; Fig. 4 and Supplementary Table 20). Three are NPR2 missense variants classified as VUSs in ClinVar but with large effects on height in our study (between −8.24 and −9.53 cm). Although none of these missense variants achieved genome-wide significance, two (p.G221R and p.R921Q) are experimentally validated loss-of-function variants44. Here we highlight large-effect variants lacking clear clinical annotations (either unannotated or classified as VUSs/CCOPs) that exemplify how population-scale association analyses provide relevant data that clinical geneticists can use to evaluate potentially disease-causing variants.

We undertook an exome-wide association study in 1,450,633 individuals, identifying 207 height-associated genes after conditioning on common variants—115 more than an earlier large-scale sequencing study9. In 17 genes, singleton pLoFs—the rarest and most deleterious variant class—were associated with absolute effects on height 52× larger than the average common variant (8.92 cm versus 0.17 cm). Although we noted substantial overlap with Mendelian syndromes, fewer than 25% (44 out of 207) of genes include a stature or skeletal growth component in their OMIM description2, and only 16% of height-increasing genes (9 out of 57) are both included in OMIM and annotated with stature or skeletal growth phenotypes. Collectively, rare variant associations showed strong concordance with genes implicated by common variant associations and reflected established biological processes influencing height, including growth factor signalling, extracellular matrix organization and transcriptional regulation.

In a recent development, our results illustrate classic trade-offs in genetic association studies between effect size and allele frequency. Expanding from singletons to low-frequency variants up to 1%, and from pLoFs to missense variants, increased the number of implicated genes from 17 to 179 but greatly diminished the average absolute effect size. Tests that more explicitly accommodate effect size heterogeneity12 or small proportions of causal variants11 within each gene increased gene discovery another 16%, bringing the total to 207 genes. As no single analysis captured all of the implicated genes, we maximized gene discovery by combining gene-based P values from multiple models using a well-calibrated omnibus gene-based test10.

The genes we found to be associated with height include those in well-understood pathways but also implicate potentially latest areas of height biology. For example, in the GH/IGF pathway, growth hormone (GH1) signals for IGF1 production, stimulating skeletal growth through cartilage generation in the growth plate45. While Mendelian syndromes with altered stature as a major feature are linked to eight members of the GH/IGF pathway—GH1, GHR, GHRHR, GHSR, IGF1, IGF1R, IGFLAS and PAPPA2 (ref. 46)—our results include seven of these eight (Supplementary Table 23), and implicate three others (PAPPA, STC2 and GHRH). Furthermore, for several genes that were previously considered to have autosomal recessive modes of inheritance (GHRHR, IGFALS, IGF1 and PAPPA2), our results show that loss-of-function and deleterious missense variants have apparent effects in the heterozygous state (Supplementary Table 23). Finally, while GH1–IGF1 is generally considered the major driver of post-natal growth and development, the IGF2 pathway is believed to act mainly during prenatal development with uncertain effects on adult height47. Human genetic evidence for a role of the IGF2 pathway in height has previously been limited to extreme short stature (>3 s.d. below average) in Silver–Russell syndrome, caused by disruptions in the IGF2 gene itself (although not implicated here)48. Our results include association in an additional IGF2 pathway gene: IGF2BP2 through singleton pLoFs (β = −8.67 cm, P = 1.52 × 10−10; Table 1), an mRNA-binding protein that stabilizes IGF2 mRNA, providing additional evidence for a developmental role of IGF signalling in adult height.

Accurate complex trait prediction is a key aspiration of human genetics. Current prediction efforts focus on common variants with effects that are individually small but substantial in aggregate. Supplementing this approach by adding both rare variants with individually large effects and burden tests provides substantial predictive value for carriers. Among 337 carriers across our 17 singleton pLoF genes, adding rare variant effects to common variant prediction models improved the prediction performance to nearly that of common variants in the full population (R2 = 0.72 in carriers versus 0.73 across the full sample). However, as these variants are so rare (<0.1% of individuals), this has a limited impact at the population level.

In a recent development, FGFR3 and PTPN11 frequently arose as interesting case studies throughout this work. First, they represent the unusual case in which rare missense variants collectively yielded a significant burden association with no contribution from pLoFs. They reduce height through GoF mechanisms22 and are known causes of achondroplasia7 and Noonan syndrome23, respectively. However, their burden effects were relatively modest (3–15× smaller; −2.31 cm for FGFR3; −4.12 cm for PTPN11) compared with the effects of a few individual variants: −29.8 cm effect for FGFR3 p.G380R; −14.2 cm for PTPN11 p.N308D; and −12.2 cm for PTPN11 p.R265Q. For most other genes, the effect sizes were more consistent for missense and pLoFs and combining them yielded the most statistically powerful analysis.

In a recent development, collectively, this work substantially expands the breadth of rare genetic associations for adult height. Beyond directly implicating 207 genes, we demonstrate how rare variant gene discovery at scale can bridge the gap between common variant GWAS and Mendelian disease genetics, providing valuable data for identifying functional genes and interpreting observed variation in clinical settings.

Our discovery analysis comprised six exome-sequenced cohorts jointly called on an Integrated DNA Technologies (IDT) modified xGen exome capture from the RGC-ME study49: the glaucoma-ascertained African Descent and Glaucoma Evaluation Study III (ADAGES; n = 1,941)50; the Mexico City Prospective Study (MCPS; n = 138,667), comprising residents from the Iztapalapa and Coyoacán districts of Mexico City35; the population-based UK Biobank (UKB; n = 452,583); and three health-system cohorts: Mount Sinai BioMe Biobank (BioMe; n = 26,850), Geisinger Health System DiscovEHR (GHS; n = 165,080)51 and Penn Medicine BioBank (PMBB; n = 40,945)52.

We performed a meta-analysis across six replication cohorts not part of the RGC-ME49. Four cohorts were exome sequenced using a TWIST capture: the household-based prospective ‘BangladEsh Longitudinal Investigation of Emerging Vascular and nonvascular Events’ (BELIEVE; n = 53,830) Study53 and three hospital-based cohorts: The Biobank at Colorado Center for Personalized Medicine (CCPM; n = 48,799)54, Mayo Clinic Project Generation (n = 72,472) and University of California Los Angeles (UCLA) at LA Study (ATLAS) Precision Health Biobank (UCLA ATLAS; n = 38,406). The longitudinal All of Us (AoU) research programme was whole-genome sequenced; participant-level phenotypic and genetic data cannot be removed from the trusted research environment and we therefore did not use AoU data for prediction analyses (AoU; n = 381,888)55. The prospective, population-based Malmö Diet and Cancer Study (MDCS; n = 29,172) was exome sequenced by IDT exome capture but could not be jointly called in the RGC-ME due to regulatory restrictions.

Industry observers note that we calculated an individual’s standing height by first converting all height measurements to centimetres, removing measurements <75 cm or taken before age 18, and then taking the median across the remaining height measurements. We excluded individuals for whom their genetically predicted sex differed from their self-reported sex as well as 76 bone marrow transplant recipients for whom their DNA was collected from blood. Within each cohort, we applied rank inverse normal transformation separately for each sex and used this rank inverse normal transformed height phenotype in genetic association analyses. To approximate height effect sizes in centimetres, we multiplied effect sizes (in s.d. units) by 7.994 cm, the sex-stratified, sample-size-weighted s.d. in the discovery cohorts.

All genomic data analysed here was generated as previous described9,49,55. In brief, exome capture was performed using IDT (ADAGES III, BioMe, GHS, MCPS, MDCS, PMBB and UKB) or TWIST (BELIEVE, CCPM, Mayo Clinic, UCLA ATLAS) capture reagents, sequencing was performed on the Illumina HiSeq 2500 or NovaSeq 6000 system, and sequencing reads were aligned to GRCh38. AoU used DNA extracted at the Mayo Clinic (blood or saliva) and sequenced at Baylor College of Medicine, Broad Institute, or University of Washington: sequencing centre and DNA source were included as batch covariates55 (Supplementary Fig. 9). PLINK (v.1.9)56 converted the pVCF to PLINK files for downstream analyses. Quality control included sample/variant missingness of <10%, ±10 bp buffer window around target regions, heterozygosity Hardy–Weinberg Equilibrium (HWE) P > 1 × 10−100, excess heterozygosity HWE P > 1 × 10−30 and setting male heterozygous genotypes in the non-pseudoautosomal region (non-PAR) of chromosome X to missing using the PLINK256 option --set-hh-missing. We implemented a previously described support vector machine (SVM)-based quality control protocol to identify likely artefactual variants9 and then used these predictions to create individual-level covariates for GWAS.

Variant Effect Predictor (VEP)57 v.100.4 (Ensembl58 release 100) annotated variants on human protein-coding transcripts and assigned a single consequence per variant based on the canonical transcript defined using MANE58, APPRIS59 and Ensembl canonical tags as previously described58.

We used REGENIE’s60 linear whole-genome regression test to perform three genetic analyses on chromosomes 1–22 and X in the discovery: (1) a TOPMed61 imputed common variant GWAS (AAF > 0.01; n = 19,527,870 variants); (2) a rare variant exome analysis (AAF ≤ 0.01, AAC ≥ 10; n = 9,086,709 variants excluding those tested in the imputed variant GWAS); and (3) a gene-based association analysis of rare coding variation (n = 19,107 gene-level omnibus tests). We set a single unified Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold of P < 1.75 × 10−9 across all three analyses, accounting for all common, rare and gene-based tests performed (0.05/28,633,686 tests). A discussion of calibration in these results is provided in the Supplementary Note.

For the non-PARs of chromosome X, we assumed a dosage-compensation model in which homozygous reference male individuals are coded as 0 and hemizygous male individuals are coded as 2 (and heterozygous male individuals were set to missing). In step 1 of REGENIE (that is, prediction of individual trait values based on genetic data), we included genotyped variants with an AAF > 1%, <10% missingness, HWE P > 10−15 and linkage-disequilibrium (LD) pruning (1,000 variant windows, 100 variant sliding windows and an r2 threshold of 0.1). The covariates used in REGENIE steps 1 and 2 are described in Supplementary Table 24.

To identify conditionally independent common GWAS variants, we performed an iterative conditional meta-analysis using REGENIE’s leave-only-same-chromosome-in (LOSCI) option on TOPMed-imputed dosage data. LOSCI conditions the variant/gene being tested only on the same-chromosome variants to avoid model overfitting. In each iteration, distance-based clumping (1 Mb minimum) identified the lead variant (P < 1.75 × 10−9), which became covariates in subsequent iterations. After 22 iterations, no variants reached significance (P < 1.75 × 10−9), yielding 3,034 independent variants used to condition all rare variant and gene-based association tests (REGENIE’s model includes each variant individually).

REGENIE collapses qualified (based on AAF and annotation) rare coding variants by gene and assigning each individual’s genotype as the maximum of their alternate alleles (2 for individuals who are homozygous alternate carriers for a qualified variant; 1 for heterozygous carriers of any qualified variant; and 0 for individuals who are homozygous reference for all qualifying variants). Burden tests were performed on these genotypes whereby effect sizes represent the per-allele effect of carrying a qualified variant. pLoFs comprised frameshift, stop gain, splice-donor or splice-acceptor variants. Missense variants were evaluated using six in silico predictors: ESM-1v62, SIFT63, PolyPhen2+HumDiv64, PolyPhen2+HumVar64, MutationTaster65 and LRT66. Variants were selected for inclusion in burden tests based on AAF, status as pLoF and—for missense variants—how many algorithms predicted the variant to be deleterious. Missense variants were classified as deleterious if predicted pathogenic by ESM-1v (using a threshold of 0.78) or all five other algorithms; and possibly deleterious if predicted to be not pathogenic by ESM-1v but predicted to be pathogenic by 1–4 other algorithms. Burden tests were then performed using every combination of five different AAF thresholds (singleton (4.17 × 10−7), 0.0001, 0.001, 0.005 and 0.01) and 7 different combinations of variant class: (1) pLoF; (2) pLoF + deleterious missense + stop lost + start lost; (3) pLoF + at least possibly deleterious missense + stop lost + start lost; (4) pLoF + all missense + stop lost + start lost; (5) deleterious missense + stop lost + start lost; (6) at least possibly deleterious missense + stop lost + start lost; and (7) all missense + stop lost + start lost—yielding 35 burden tests.

Recent findings suggest that to properly adjust for multiple correlated tests across a large number of genes, we used gene-P10, an omnibus gene-based test framework that uses ACAT67 to combine P values from four complementary rare variant gene-based tests—BURDEN-ACAT10, Sparse Burden Association Test (SBAT)10, SKAT-O12 and ACAT-V11—into a single P value per gene (Supplementary Fig. 1) as previously described10. After identifying genes associated through gene-P, we quantified the number of significant associations from these four underlying tests (Extended Data Fig. 1a). We classified genes into two groups: burden-associated (P < 1.75 × 10−9 in BURDEN-ACAT or SBAT) or non-burden-associated (P < 1.75 × 10−9 in ACAT-V or SKAT-O and P ≥ 1.75 × 10−9 in both BURDEN-ACAT and SBAT).

Sources indicate that we used a previously described method for genetic ancestry assignment49. In brief, using a diverse reference panel comprising 11,354 individuals from 95 populations, we calculated the proportion of haplotype sharing of each sample and assigned them to one of six genetic ancestries (African (AFR), Indigenous American (AMR), East Asian (EAS), European (EUR), Middle Eastern (MEA), and South Asian (SAS)) if they had greater than 50% of that genetic ancestry; those with no majority ancestry were assigned to an ‘OTH’ group. We recognize that these commonly used labels oversimplify an individual’s genetic, cultural and environmental diversity, and use them only out of convenience to properly adjust association tests for genetic ancestry.

It has been revealed that in both imputed and sequenced data, we assigned each variant a single AAF representing the maximum AAF across six fine-scale ancestries. On the basis of the fine-scale ancestry maximum AAF, we classified variants as common (AAF ≥ 1%; n = 19,514,636 in imputed data with INFO ≥ 0.3 in all discovery cohorts) or rare (AAF < 1%; n = 44,600,231 in exome data). When a variant was rare (<1%) in the exome, but common in the imputed data (≥1%), we classified them as common (n = 335,522). Singletons in the discovery analysis were defined as those with only a single AAC for variants on chromosomes 1–22 and the X chromosome’s PAR, and a single hemizygous or heterozygous genotype in the X chromosome’s non-PAR. REGENIE used these AAFs and singleton definitions when writing burden test genotypes and running the gene-based tests (options --aaf-file and --set-singleton). For replication analyses, we used the same AAFs as in the discovery analysis but included an additional 12,777,247 unique variants in the replication data. Singletons in the replication comprised variants that were either (1) a singleton in the discovery or (2) a singleton in the replication that was absent from the discovery.

We compared the pLoF burden effect sizes to common variants identified by GWAS at the same genes by linking conditionally independent GWAS variants to their nearest gene through genomic distance. For genes with multiple nearby GWAS variants, we computed the mean absolute GWAS effect size. For each gene g with kg GWAS loci (where kg > 0), we computed the ratio of the singleton absolute pLoF effect size to the GWAS conditional joint effect size. Specifically, for gene g with singleton pLoF absolute effect size |\({{\beta }}_{g}^{\mathrm{pLoF}}\)| and a set of GWAS conditional joint effect sizes \({\beta }_{1}^{\mathrm{GWAS}}\), \({\beta }_{2}^{\mathrm{GWAS}}\), … , \({\beta }_{{k}_{g}}^{\mathrm{GWAS}}\), we defined the per-gene ratio as:.

Industry observers note that these ratios quantify the fold-increase in phenotypic effect conferred by complete gene disruption (through a singleton pLoF carried by an individual) relative to the effect of common regulatory or coding variation at the same locus identified through GWAS. Ratios of >1 indicate that the singleton pLoF has a larger effect on height than the nearby common GWAS variant, consistent with the expectation that rare, gene-disrupting variants tend to have larger per-allele effect sizes than common variants due to stronger purifying selection.

We built a common variant PGS using PLINK56 from 3,039 common (Supplementary Table 8) variants from two sources: first, 3,034 conditionally independent common variants identified through iterative conditional meta-analysis (Methods and Supplementary Table 2) and second, five common variants identified from the exome and not tested with imputed data. The common variant PGS was computed as a weighted sum of alternate alleles, where the magnitude and direction of the weight was based on the estimated variant effect size (in s.d. units) from a joint model in the discovery (n = 826,066; Supplementary Table 1) of all 3,039 variants (Supplementary Table 8) and the same covariates (Supplementary Table 24) used in the association analyses (Supplementary Note).

We constructed four versions of rare variant PGS (rvPGS), based on the 179 genes with a significant gene-P and either a significant BURDEN-ACAT or SBAT test, weighted using s.d. effect sizes: (1) rvPGSSNP: all 77 significant (P < 1.75 × 10−9, AAC ≥ 10) rare variants in these genes (after LD clumping for variants with R2 < 0.2), weighted by the single-variant effect size; (2) rvPGSpLoF: all 179 pLoF (AAF < 1%, AAC ≥ 10) burden associations weighted by effect size; (3) rvPGSmissense: all 179 deleterious missense (AAF < 1%, AAC ≥ 10) burden associations weighted by effect size; and (4) rvPGSsynonymous: all 179 synonymous (AAF < 1%, AAC ≥ 10) burden associations weighted by effect size. When predicting height based on both rvPGSSNP and burden-based rvPGS, both the burden genotypes and burden effect sizes were recomputed to exclude the variants included in the single-variant rvPGS to enforce independence between the rvPGS.

All estimations of variance explained by the PGS were performed using genes and effect sizes from the discovery (n = 826,066) but estimated using the replication (n = 242,679 excluding AoU; Supplementary Table 1). First, for each cohort–sex combination (five cohorts × two sexes), a linear regression model was fit of height (in centimetres) on the covariates used in the replication association tests. The PGS of interest was added into the model, and the variance explained was calculated as the difference in adjusted R2 between the two nested models. The reported value was the mean of the ten cohort–sex subsets (five cohorts × two sexes). When computing variance explained by rare-variant PGS, the null model included the 3,039 common variant PGSs (Supplementary Table 8) in addition to covariates (Supplementary Table 24) mentioned above.

Recent findings suggest that in replication cohorts (n = 242,679; excluding AoU; Supplementary Table 1), we predicted an individual’s height (in centimetres) from a mean-centred common variant PGS in s.d. units as follows:.

where \({\bar{\mathrm{height}}}_{\mathrm{cohort},\mathrm{sex}}\) and \({\text{s.d.}}_{\mathrm{cohort},\mathrm{sex}}\) are the mean and s.d. of height among replication individuals matched on cohort and sex.

Sources indicate that although height differs by genetic ancestry, we did not stratify predictions explicitly by genetic ancestry to avoid excluding small subpopulations (Supplementary Table 1). However, most replication cohorts (excluding AoU) comprised individuals of a single genetic ancestry, so stratification by cohort was effectively the same as stratifying by genetic ancestry.

According to recent reports, to predict an individual’s height using rare variants, we calculated various rvPGS using the 179 gene-P genes with significant burden-ACAT or SBAT P value. Owing to the nested nature of burden tests with respect to AAF (for example, a burden test of <1% AAF variants also includes all the variants in a singleton burden test), we restricted to only selecting a specific AAF for each class of variants. We also ensured that in any predictive models including both burden and significant single variants, the burden effects were recomputed without any significant single variants. rvPGS tested include: pLoF AAF < 1%, deleterious missense AAF < 1%, all significant rare variants, height predictions incorporating rare variant PGS (rvPGS) were calculated as:.

To assess the accuracy of any PGS, we report the R2 of a univariate linear model of predicted height on observed height.

The Loss-of-function observed/expected upper bound fraction (LOEUF) metric follows a uniform distribution18 and was available for 201 out of 207 gene-P genes (all but FGD1, HDAC6, IRS4, NRK, SCMH1 and SHOX). We considered genes to be LoF-constrained if they were in the first LOEUF quintile. When comparing whether two gene sets significantly differed with respect to LOEUF, we used a Wilcoxon rank-sum test on LOEUF ranks.

In a recent development, to assess whether height-associated genes identified through rare variant burden testing were enriched for biologically relevant annotations—OMIM disease genes (all and stature/skeletal growth-related, curated in ref. 2), constrained genes and nearest gene to a GWAS signal—we used two-sided Fisher’s exact tests to test for enrichment; when odds ratios were infinite due to zero count cells, we applied a continuity correction of +1 to all cells.

To address potential confounding by coding sequence (CDS) length, whereby longer genes may be more likely to contain rare qualifying variants and reach significance, we performed a canonical CDS-length-matched enrichment analysis. For each gene, we identified the five closest background genes by canonical CDS length, sampled without replacement, to construct a null set and repeated all analyses described above using these CDS-matched background genes.

Recent findings suggest that we used a two-sided 2 × 2 Fisher’s exact test to assess whether individuals carrying rare variants were more likely to be observed in the subset of the population based on various thresholds (in s.d. units) of either their predictive error (that is, the absolute difference in the observed and common-variant predicted height; Supplementary Table 18) or their observed height (Supplementary Table 19). The set of genes that we examined included either genes with a significant (P < 1.75 × 10−9) burden test (for example, 17 genes from singleton pLoF burden tests, 8 genes from singleton deleterious burden tests; Fig. 1b and Supplementary Table 6) or all significant gene-P genes with a significant SBAT or burden-ACAT test (Fig. 1d and Supplementary Table 4). While varying the variant class, AAF threshold, gene set and s.d. threshold, we kept the comparison group constant, defaulting to <0.5 s.d. from the mean.

When comparing height association results to ClinVar, height association statistics from the meta-analysis of the discovery and replication cohorts (n = 1.45 million) were used to maximize sample size. For consistency, the list of gene-P genes used for subsetting variants was the list of 207 genes from the discovery only (Supplementary Table 4). ClinVar data were downloaded in July 2025. To subset for diseases with a stature-related component, the union of three filters was used:.

String matching of ClinVar disease column for any of the following strings: stature, height or chondroplasia.

Searching for any of the following manually curated, height-related Human Phenotype Ontology terms in the list of observed phenotype codes: HP:0004322, HP:0003510, HP:0001519, HP:0003498, HP:0003508, HP:0008909, HP:0003502, HP:0008845, HP:0008857, HP:0008848, HP:0011405, HP:0011406, HP:0011404, HP:0011407, HP:0000098, HP:0008873, HP:0003521, HP:0008921, HP:0008922, HP:0008929, HP:0008905, HP:0000002.

In a recent development, searching the observed phenotype codes for 506 height-related MONDO terms (Supplementary Table 25). This list was generated by MONDO label, definition and synonym fields for the strings stature, height and chondroplasia, and removing any field with the string normal stature.

Any ClinVar entry meeting at least one of these criteria was included in the analysis, yielding 47,763 variants before filtering for those in gene-P genes. While not comprehensive (several variants in Supplementary Table 21 affect known height genes but are not included), this list identifies a set of variants in ClinVar for which the listed diseases are confidently determined to involve stature. Enrichment testing for significant variants in each ClinVar pathogenicity bin (Supplementary Table 22) was performed using the binomial test (probability of success = 1.75 × 10−9).

The following data resources are available by application: All of Us Research Program Controlled Tier Dataset Release 8 (https://www.researchallofus.org/), BELIEVE study (https://believestudy-bangladesh.org/accessing-believe-data/), BioMe (https://mountsinaimillion.org/en/contact), CCPM (https://medschool.cuanschutz.edu/cobiobank/contact-us), GHS (https://regeneron.envisionpharma.com/vt_regeneron/), Project Generation Mayo Clinic Biobank (https://www.mayo.edu/research/centers-programs/mayo-clinic-biobank/for-researchers), MDCS (https://www.malmo-kohorter.lu.se/malmo-cohorts), PMBB (https://pmbb.med.upenn.edu/contact.php) and UK Biobank (http://www.ukbiobank.ac.uk/register-apply/). Data from the MCPS are available to researchers on application. The MCPS Data Sample Sharing policy is available in English and Spanish at https://www.ctsu.ox.ac.uk/research/mcps; metadata describing the available datasets can be examined through the Data Showcase (https://datashare.ndph.ox.ac.uk/mexico); and MCPS ancestry-specific allele frequencies are available at https://rgc-mcps.regeneron.com. Privacy regulations prohibit individual-level UCLA-ATLAS data from being published, although processed data and summary statistics are available in the Supplementary Tables or through the UCLA-ATLAS browser (https://atlas-phewas.mednet.ucla.edu). Genetic variation for all discovery cohorts (ADAGES III, BioMe, GHS, MCPS, PMBB, UKB) are made publicly available through the RGC Million Exome Browser (https://rgc-research.regeneron.com/me/home). The list of 12,111 COJO SNPs and 462 OMIM height and skeletal growth-related genes were downloaded from supplementary tables 10 and 11 of ref. 2, respectively (https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41586-022-05275-y/MediaObjects/41586_2022_5275_MOESM3_ESM.xlsx). GIANT GWAS summary statistics were downloaded from the Broad Institute: (https://giant-consortium.web.broadinstitute.org/index.php/GIANT_consortium_data_files#2022_GWAS_Summary_Statistics_and_Polygenic_Score_.28PGS.29_Weights). LOEUF scores (gnomAD v.4.1) for constraint were downloaded from the Broad Institute (https://gnomad.broadinstitute.org/downloads). ClinVar annotations were downloaded in July 2025 (https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pub/clinvar/).

Industry observers note that a, UpSet plot decomposing the 207 genes identified by gene-P into the four underlying gene-based test methods: SBAT, BURDEN-ACAT, SKAT-O, or ACAT-V. The union of SBAT and BURDEN-ACAT yielded 179 genes which we defined as burden genes. UpSet plots for the 179 burden genes broken down by (b) variant class and (c) AAF threshold.

Forty-one variants with AAF < 0.01% are shown. The dashed black line indicates no effect, and the solid red line indicates the burden effect size when aggregating all the variants in the figure (β = −3.1 cm).

Each point represents a group of burden tests of a given type (specified by colour) that meet a given P-value threshold. Proportion of negative synonymous burden tests with P < 1.75×10−9 (n < 5) not shown. Two-sided burden P-values were calculated by REGENIE. Point estimates represent observed proportions and error bars represent 95% confidence intervals around these estimates. Vertical bars indicate the number of genes included in each estimate.

It has been revealed that estimated using burden heritability regression (BHR) in discovery data (n = 826,066 individuals). Point estimates represent the mean cumulative heritability estimates for each variant annotation and frequency range. Error bars represent 95% confidence intervals around these point estimates.

Variance explained is calculated as the difference in adjusted R2 between nested linear models of height: one with only common variants and covariates and one that also includes a rare variant PGS. Each point represents all burden tests of a given type (specified by colour) that meet the given P-value threshold (the number of burden tests in each point is given in Extended Data Fig. 3). Two-sided burden association statistics were calculated by REGENIE. Likelihood Ratio Test (LRT) used to determine whether the variance explained by rare variant burden tests was significantly different from zero at a conservative, Bonferroni-corrected α=0.0001 to adjust for 500 tests performed.

Solid vertical lines represent mean values for each prediction method; black dashed line indicates no difference between observed and predicted height. All individuals shown are in replication data.

Variants (AAF < 0.1%) are separated by ClinVar pathogenicity. Black dashed lines indicate a Z-score of 0 and red dashed lines indicate the Z-score threshold corresponding to P = 1.75×10−9 (Z = ± 6.02). Two-sided single-variant association statistics were calculated by REGENIE. Red numbers represent the number of variants with Z scores more extreme than the genome-wide threshold.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Nolan | 25 Nov 2026 23:52, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 04:58.

The City Ground will be the backdrop for a clash that will impact the race for Europe and the relegation battle in the Premier League table, when Chelsea visit Nottingham Forest on Friday.

The Garibaldis are hoping to bounce back from defeat at the weekend, while the Blues are desperate to avoid a third loss in a row.

Oliver Glasner's Nottingham Forest have endured a dire campaign to date, and they will be fighting to stay out of the bottom three this week.

The Tricky Trees are right now 17th with nine points to their name, only above 18th-placed Sunderland on goal difference, as well as a single point ahead of 19th-placed Manchester United, and just two clear of bottom club Crystal Palace.

Glasner's side shocked the Premier League by beating Manchester City 3-1 on November 7, courtesy of a sixth-minute opener from Cunha and a brace from Liam Delap.

However, Forest failed to build on what was just their second win of the top-flight season, falling to a 2-0 defeat at Bournemouth on Saturday.

That loss marked the sixth time that the Garibaldis have blanked in 11 league matches this term, and only Sunderland have scored fewer than their tally of nine goals so far.

Meanwhile, Xabi Alonso arrived at Chelsea knowing that he had his work cut out to right the ship, but the Londoners travel to the City Ground in particularly poor form.

On Saturday, the Blues were thrashed 4-1 by Leeds United at Stamford Bridge, a stunning result in its own right made worse by the fact Emmanuel Emegha had given Chelsea the lead midway through the first half.

That defeat was a fourth in five games for Alonso's side, who were also beaten 1-0 by struggling Sunderland at the Stadium of Light prior to the international break.

Adding to the growing concern at the club is the fact that Chelsea have now conceded 20 goals in the top flight, meaning that promoted Coventry City and Ipswich Town are the only teams outside of the relegation zone to have let in more this term.

Now eighth in the Premier League table with 16 points, the Blues are five behind fourth-placed Liverpool, but still have fifth-placed Bournemouth in their sights just two points in front.

However, Alonso will also be looking over his shoulder on Friday, given that his side are within reach of every club down to 13th-placed Newcastle United, and another defeat could see them drop into the bottom half.

Nottingham Forest Premier League form:.

Chelsea form (all competitions):.

Forest are without Nicolo Savona once again as he recovers from a knee injury, though Daniel Munoz should be on hand to start at right wing-back, flanking Glasner's three-man defence.

The Tricky Trees are also missing midfielder Nicolas Dominguez, who has been dealing with a muscle injury, so Xaver Schlager and James McAtee could operate in the centre of the park on Friday.

On a more positive note, the hosts are set to welcome former Chelsea star Callum Hudson-Odoi back after he returned to training this week, and he is likely to offer additional firepower from the bench while Morgan Gibbs-White and Dan Ndoye line up behind striker Liam Delap.

As for Chelsea, they have doubts about midfielder Moises Caicedo, who was forced off with a back issue against Leeds, and winger Jamie Gittens, who has returned to training but is still building fitness after his layoff.

With that in mind, Pedro Neto, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers should start behind Emmanuel Emegha, given that talismanic centre-forward Joao Pedro is sidelined due to a thigh injury.

At the opposite end of the pitch, versatile right-back Reece James has a knee injury, left-sided defender Jorrel Hato is out with a back glitch, and centre-half Maxence Lacroix is recovering from a hamstring injury.

In their absence, Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill will operate at the heart of Alonso's defence, while Josh Acheampong and Pep Chavarria start at full-back.

Nottingham Forest possible starting lineup:.

Sels; Cunha, Milenkovic, Murillo; Munoz, McAtee, Schlager, Williams; Gibbs-White, Ndoye; Delap.

Chelsea possible starting lineup:.

Martinez; Acheampong, Fofana, Colwill, Chavarria; Henderson, Lavia; Neto, Palmer, Rogers; Emegha.

Forest have struggled for goals this season, but they will be motivated by the threat of slipping into the relegation zone, and given optimism by the visitors' poor form.

Chelsea arrive on the back of four defeats in five games, desperate to find their feet amidst a spate of injuries, though it would come as no surprise to see the Blues drop points once again.

What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1069 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For the millions who cast their ballots in the US midterm elections, one matter ranked above all others: the economy.
  • So what does the Democrats' stunning capture of both the US Senate and House of Representatives mean for the economy and economic policy, given that President Donald Trump still has two years of his term to go?
  • According to recent reports, markets have rebounded after initially trending negatively.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the millions who cast their ballots in the US midterm elections, one matter ranked above all others: the economy.

So what does the Democrats' stunning capture of both the US Senate and House of Representatives mean for the economy and economic policy, given that President Donald Trump still has two years of his term to go?

According to recent reports, markets have rebounded after initially trending negatively. Global stocks rallied as investors appeared to take heart from the Democrats' victory.

In a recent development, with Democrats now holding comfortable majorities in both houses of Congress and Trump still in the White House, it could lead to gridlock in Washington. Trump has already said he would become "Mr Veto," meaning he would block any legislation the Democrats advance.

"The magnitude of the gains for the Democrats in the midterms does not change too much for the near-term policy outlook, given the party still lacks a filibuster-proof majority in the Senate and President Trump has veto power to block legislation," Stephen Brown, chief North America economist with Capital Economics, remarked in a note.

It has been revealed that "I think we are looking at two years of complete 100% gridlock," Jacob Funk Kirkegaard, nonresident senior fellow with the Peterson Institute for International Economics, told DW after the results came in. "Nothing will get done of any kind.".

It has been revealed that some investors appear worried that the Democrats could force through AI regulation, especially if they also win the White House in 2028. Rising opposition among large majorities of the US population to data centers — the key infrastructure behind AI — helped secure victories for many Democratic candidates.

Kirkegaard, who is also a senior fellow at Bruegel, a European economics think tank, noted the vote showed the extent of that opposition. Even if the Democrats can't force regulation, he thinks local opposition will make it harder for data centers to be built, which could hit the valuation of big tech firms that have benefitted from the AI boom.

"This election indicates that the political underpinning of the rapid, aggressive AI growth story is shaky," he noted. "It doesn't mean it's going to stop or be made illegal, but the dynamic of the growth story has shifted.".

If the Democrats were to win the presidency in 2028, Brown noted, they would be perfectly placed to make major policy changes. "That includes the potential for tax hikes on corporations and high-income individuals as well as regulation that could delay the AI rollout," he said.

According to polling conducted in early October by the Pew Research Center, 56% of Americans say Trump's tariff policies will have mostly negative impacts on the country, with only 20% saying mostly positive.

Sources indicate that that sentiment clearly drove many Democrats to victory in the midterms — particularly in states where tariffs have had a particularly negative impact. That includes those with sectors reliant on exports, such as Texas, Michigan, Iowa and Illinois, where counter-tariffs have hit and those that have high trade volumes with Canada.

Yet, barring an unprecedented climbdown from Trump — who has been ideologically wedded to tariffs since he first became a public figure almost 50 years ago — it's not clear how the Democrats could force substantial change to the president's signature economic policy.

Sources indicate that "Trump will not be moderated," Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Hinrich Foundation in Singapore, told DW earlier this year. "Expect him to continue his trade disruption and tariff policies for as long as he remains in the Oval Office.".

Though the US Constitution gives Congress the power to collect and organize tariffs, various laws passed over the years have given presidents power to implement tariffs when they cite certain conditions, such as national security or economic emergencies.

According to recent reports, trump has already used such avenues for his tariffs and can continue to do so, despite some legal rebukes. However, while Congress can't necessarily force an end to Trump's existing tariffs, it can now take further legal action against them to prevent greater escalation.

Though Trump and the Democrats are clearly not going to make common cause, Kirkegaard noted, the scale of the Republicans' defeat might force Trump to be less erratic in his policymaking, from escalating his trade war with Canada to his Iran policy.

Trump stated in the aftermath of Tuesday's defeats that he would "work with" the Democrats and told the Financial Times in the run-up to the vote that he was unlikely to escalate the war in Iran.

Were a deal to be struck with Iran, soaring energy prices — a pivotal election concern — could finally fall, helping voters with their cost-of-living concerns.

"You've got to get a deal with Iran, and you've got to bring down gas prices," Kirkegaard mentioned. "From a political point of view, that's the most notable thing now.".

George Saravelos, an analyst with Deutsche Bank FX Research, thinks the markets are beginning to become more optimistic in that area. "With oil flows through the Middle East having materially recovered, the market is pricing a large imminent risk premium of re-escalation and energy supply disruption," he said in a note.

Despite the scale of the Democrats' victory, the fact that Trump remains in the Oval Office will complicate all efforts to force a change to signature economic policies and issues.

Yet Congress can now exert considerable pressure. Another concern vital to voters was corruption and the belief that the Trump administration has engaged in corruption and personal enrichment while in office.

That raises the prospect of the new Democratic-controlled Congress launching legal investigations and potentially pursuing another impeachment of Trump, which could force the president to negotiate on some economic issues to secure his political survival.

In a recent development, "Can you find 10 or 12 Republican senators who, in the face of overwhelming corruption, would be willing to vote for articles of impeachment? I wouldn't rule it out," Kirkegaard noted. "And that's a scenario in which Trump might suddenly be much more accommodating to, for instance, abandoning most of his tariffs.".

Despite voters' clear rejection of Trump's economic policies, the Democratic Party's newly minted senators, congressmen and congresswomen face an uphill battle in trying to reverse them.

Nicolas Jackson has six league goals and gives the visitor a credible threat against a defense conceding two per game.

The main uncertainty is whether Villa can recover its rhythm after the trip to Turkey. Ipswich’s willingness to attack at home should provide space, but the visitor will also need to protect its own box more convincingly than it did in midweek.

By Lewis Nolan | 25 Nov 2026 23:55.

Liverpool are seriously considering re-signing Jarell Quansah from Bayer Leverkusen in 2027, the latest report has claimed.

Andoni Iraola's side emerged as 3-0 winners against Club Brugge in the Champions League on Wednesday, with the Merseysiders keeping a second consecutive clean sheet.

Captain Virgil van Dijk started on the bench, before coming on to add more solidity at the back alongside Jeremy Jacquet.

Van Dijk has been exceptional once again this season, but with his contract set to expire at the end of the current campaign, Iraola could soon be in the market for a replacement.

TEAMtalk have claimed that former Red Quansah has emerged as a serious target, though Liverpool's buy-back clause of £50m will expire after the coming summer transfer window, meaning a decision about signing him will have to be made in the coming months.

Quansah is a strong passer of the ball ane has demonstrated in the past that he is capable of coming out on top in battles in the air, though he has struggled to settle this season.

In the 2026-27 Bundesliga, the centre-back has only completed 42.3 passes per match and has won just 32% of his aerial duels, something that may be a major concern to Liverpool given he is 6ft 3in.

The 23-year-old completed 52.8 passes per game last season in the league, while he also won 60% of his aerial duels.

There are concerns about Quansah's recovery defending and temperament inside the box, so perhaps Liverpool should look elsewhere in the summer for the heir to Van Dijk.

The unfortunate reality for Liverpool is that they will have to become accustomed to life without Van Dijk sooner rather than later.

However, there is nothing to suggest based on his current form that the 35-year-old cannot continue to play at the highest level for at least another season.

As long as Van Dijk can continue to dominate attackers and use his immense recovery pace, then Liverpool should look to extend their captain's contract.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cristiano Ronaldo took to social media on Thursday to announce that he had played his last game for Portugal.

"To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the No. 7 shirt of our national team," the 41-year-old Ronaldo said in a video on his Instagram account.

"I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world," Ronaldo said.

The former Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus forward represented his country 234 times, scoring 146 goals — making him the men's record-holder for ⁠international ​appearances and for international goals.

He captained Portugal ​to their first major trophy at ​Euro 2016 and led them to the 2019 and 2025 Nations League titles.

"It was not an easy decision, there are decisions that are not ​only with the head. They are also made with the heart," Ronaldo continued in the Instagram post.

"If I ever made you happy, ​if one of my goals ever made you hug someone, forget a worry or feel ⁠proud ​of our country, then it ​was all worth it.".

He also thanked his family, the Portuguese people ​and the teammates, coaches and staff he worked with over his national ​team career.

The Portuguese Football Association (FPF) released a statement expressing its gratitude and respect for the player also known as "CR7.".

"Cristiano Ronaldo has raised Portugal's profile and inspired generations of young people who dream of following in his footsteps; for many of us, he is the greatest player of all time!" it read.

The FPF intends to organize a tribute "in which the fans and the country can one more time applaud and celebrate a player who has given us so much.".

It has been revealed that while his long-rival Lionel Messi ended his Argentina career with a much anticipated farewell match last month, Ronaldo's final appearance may go down as Portugal's 1-0 win over Wales on September 24, depending on the nature of the tribute. Portugal coach Jorge Jesus left him on the bench for the following match and said he wouldn't start the next one.

Industry observers note that ronaldo responded by walking out of the Portugal training camp. He was subsequently suspended and fined by the FPF, but he had been expected to return to Portugal for the November international break.

Like Messi, Ronaldo intends to continue his club career with Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Surprise Serie A pace-setters Lazio head to Turin on Saturday night looking to maintain their position at the top of the table when they take on Torino at the Stadio Olimpico Grande Torino.

While the visitors have not lost a league match since the start of the season and are beginning to attract genuine Scudetto talk, Torino enter the weekend battling to halt a four-match winless run that has dragged them toward the lower half of the standings.

Torino’s campaign has been one of peaks and troughs under new head coach Ignazio Abate.

Sources indicate that after a difficult start to the season, the Granata appeared to turn a corner by recording three consecutive Serie A victories. However, that momentum has faded rapidly, and they now find themselves without a win in four matches. Their latest setback came last weekend in a 1-0 defeat away to Napoli, leaving them with just one point from their last four outings.

As a result, Torino find themselves closer to the relegation zone than the European places, despite showing signs of promise earlier in the campaign.

In a recent development, home form has become a particular concern. Torino have conceded nearly two goals per game on their own turf this season and are at the moment on a club-record run of 11 consecutive Serie A home matches without a clean sheet. Those defensive issues will be under intense scrutiny against the league’s most in-form side.

Sources indicate that there is, however, some hope in the recent head-to-head record. Torino defeated Lazio 2-0 in the corresponding fixture last March and could record consecutive victories over the Biancocelesti for the first time since 2013.

Torino’s attacking hopes will largely rest on Che Adams, who has scored four Serie A goals this season, alongside Giovanni Simeone, a player with an impressive record against Lazio. The Argentine has scored 10 league goals against the Roman club during his career and will be hoping to add to that tally on Saturday.

Defensively, the hosts have suffered a setback with Ardian Ismajli, who suffered an adductor injury during the defeat to Napoli and has subsequently undergone surgery.

According to recent reports, abate is also dealing with fitness concerns involving wing-backs Rafik Belghali and Ricardo Rodriguez. Belghali continues to struggle with knee inflammation, meaning Zakaria Aboukhlal, Nicolo Fortini or even Nathan Patterson could feature on the right flank.

Lazio continue to defy expectations at the summit of Serie A.

According to recent reports, since beginning Gennaro Gattuso’s reign with a shock Coppa Italia defeat to Mantova, the Biancocelesti have been outstanding. They have dropped only four points across their first 12 league matches and head into the weekend three points clear of reigning champions Inter and two ahead of city rivals Roma.

Victory in Turin would give Lazio 11 wins from their opening 13 matches, matching a pace not seen since Napoli’s title-winning 2022-23 campaign.

Recent findings suggest that their most recent success came against Lecce, where Tijjani Noslin scored twice before Davide Frattesi added a memorable chipped finish to complete the victory. Those performances have helped fuel growing belief among supporters that Lazio could challenge for a first Scudetto in 27 years.

Gattuso will be keen to keep those ambitions grounded, however, knowing that a difficult trip to Turin awaits before next month’s potentially decisive Derby della Capitale against Roma.

With Lazio no longer involved in other competitions, Gattuso has generally played a settled side, although he is at the moment without two vital defensive players.

In a recent development, both Nuno Tavares and Josip Sutalo remain sidelined with flexor injuries. There is better news regarding captain Mattia Zaccagni, who has resumed full training and could return to the matchday squad after missing recent action.

Davide Frattesi enters the fixture as Lazio’s leading Serie A scorer with five goals, while Tijjani Noslin has been one of the division’s form players, recording at least one goal involvement in each of his last four appearances.

This fixture pits two sides moving in opposite directions. Lazio have developed into one of the most consistent teams in Italy under Gattuso, while Torino have struggled for results in recent weeks and continue to battle defensive complications, particularly at home.

Although Torino can take confidence from their victory in the reverse fixture last season, current form strongly favours the visitors. With Lazio conceding fewer than one goal per game on average and boasting several players in excellent attacking form, they appear well equipped to continue their impressive unbeaten run.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

The FA publicly backed Tuchel after the defeat by Argentina, but the German has now revealed that he was privately told his job was safe well before that.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The ruling follows a controversial final in which Senegal initially won 1-0 after extra time, only for the result to be overturned following an appeal to Confederation of African Football (CAF) by the Moroccan Football Federation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 09:30 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:47 EST, 24 November 2026.

Senegal have been reinstated as Africa Cup of Nations winners after succeeding with an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), ten months after they beat Morocco in Rabat.

The ruling follows a controversial final in which Senegal initially won 1-0 after extra time, only for the result to be overturned following an appeal to Confederation of African Football (CAF) by the Moroccan Football Federation.

Two months after the final, the CAF appeal board ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match because their players had walked off the pitch in protest over a controversial penalty decision.

In a recent development, morocco were subsequently awarded a 3-0 victory and the title. Despite that, Senegal refused to hand the trophy over.

That decision was based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, which state that leaving the pitch constitutes a forfeit.

However, following an appeal to CAS, Senegal have been reinstalled as champions, with the court ruling that FIFA's law that the referee’s decision is final takes precedence over the competition regulations.

Therefore, because the officials did not enforce the competition regulations at the time, there were no grounds to overturn the result.

The Moroccan FA, though, have not given up and have vowed to take the matter beyond CAS after questioning the integrity of panelist Ulrich Haas.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has restored Senegal as Africa Cup of Nations winners after they were successful in their appeal.

Morocco were awarded a 3-0 victory two months after the final, after it was ruled Senegal had forfeited the match by walking off the pitch in protest over a late penalty decision.

Senegal fans clashed with security in Rabat after the controversial penalty decision.

Ruling in favour of Senegal on Tuesday, CAS said: 'In the Panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the Referee’s decision were limited to the pitch.

'As such, the Panel considers that the Referee’s decision was covered by the "field of play" doctrine.

'Since Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently, they are therefore not applicable in this case.'.

Sources indicate that A statement from the Moroccan FA later added: 'We take note of the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport regarding the appeal filed by the Senegalese Football Federation against the decision of the CAF Appeals Committee, relating to the final match of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. In this context, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation expresses its surprise and protest at the failure to take into account its demand to arrange the necessary legal consequences for practices that would compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration procedure, especially what has been confirmed regarding communication between the German referee Ulrich Haas (who sat on the CAS panel) and the president of the Senegalese Football Federation, 48 hours before the decision was issued.

'The Royal Moroccan Football Federation also notes that the decision did not take into account the approach recently adopted by both the International Football Association Board (IFAB) and FIFA, regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee’s permission, and the resulting disciplinary responsibilities and penalties.

'Accordingly, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation confirms its intention to pursue all available legal avenues to appeal the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport.'.

The chaos was triggered by events at the end of normal time, when referee Jean Jacques Ndala awarded Morocco a contentious penalty in the 98th minute after being called to the monitor by the video assistant referee to review El Hadji Malick Diouf’s challenge on Brahim Diaz.

The decision came just minutes after Senegal had seen a goal ruled out.

Furious with the penalty decision, Senegal manager Pape Thiaw instructed his players to leave the pitch in protest.

After a 17-minute delay, the team eventually returned, with former Liverpool forward Sadio Mane earning praise for remaining on the pitch and encouraging his teammates to continue.

In the dramatic aftermath, Real Madrid forward Brahim Diaz saw his Panenka penalty stopped by Senegal goalkeeper Edouard Mendy, before Ndala brought normal time to an end.

Senegal went on to score early in extra time, which has now led to a second title in the past three editions of the tournament with their 1-0 victory eventually confirmed in the courtroom.

Russia is back in world sport, but who is drug testing its athletes?

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Two-time European champion Anastasiia Romanova, who previously served a two-year doping ban, was among those not tested by the ITA during the first nine months of 2026, according to its quarterly anti-doping reports.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fresh questions have emerged over Russia's return to world sport after figures reviewed by DW indicated that only four of the 16 Russian weightlifters competing at this year's world championships underwent out-of-competition testing by the International Testing Agency (ITA).

Two-time European champion Anastasiia Romanova, who previously served a two-year doping ban, was among those not tested by the ITA during the first nine months of 2026, according to its quarterly anti-doping reports.

By comparison, all 13 members of the North Korean team underwent at least one ITA test during the same period. North Korea, like Russia, has a history of doping violations in weightlifting.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The ITA, which runs weightlifting's anti-doping program, told DW that it tested all 16 Russian weightlifters "ahead of their participation in the event." DW understands those tests were conducted in Ningbo, China, where the championships are being held.

Sources indicate that in a power sport like weightlifting, performance-enhancing drugs are most beneficial during training, when athletes build strength and muscle mass in the months before competition. Some drugs, such as anabolic steroids, may be harder to detect by the time the competition comes around.

Rob Koehler, head of the athlete-led movement Global Athlete, called the lack of out-of-competition testing "absurd.".

Recent findings suggest that "Out-of-competition testing is the backbone of anti-doping," Koehler told DW. "Everybody knows there's going to be testing at the event. But not everybody knows when they're going to be tested 365 days a year outside events. It's concerning that the ITA doesn't see this as a red flag.".

Marta Nawrocka, the ITA's spokesperson, noted that Russian athletes were among the 10 most-tested nationalities in weightlifting this year. She also defended the fact that only two Russian weightlifters feature in the sport's highest-priority testing pool, saying inclusion is based on performance and risk profiles.

"Russia's history of doping in weightlifting remains an key factor in the ITA's risk assessment and testing priorities," Nawrocka said. "Russian weightlifters remain subject to substantial testing activity.".

Koehler, though, is unconvinced.

Industry observers note that "You simply can't treat Russia like any other country," he said. "It has to have more scrutiny. It has to have more testing. If you don't do that, you're undermining athlete confidence in the system.".

The International Weightlifting Federation did not respond to a request for comment.

Industry observers note that weightlifting was one of the sports most implicated in Russia's state-sponsored doping scandal, which came to light after the 2014 Sochi Winter Olympics. It ranked second only to athletics for the number of positive cases identified by Canadian lawyer Richard McLaren in his 2016 report commissioned by WADA, the global anti-doping watchdog.

It has been revealed that the scandal led to dozens of Russian athletes being banned across numerous sports. RUSADA, Russia's anti-doping agency, has remained suspended for most of the past decade.

As a result, its Moscow laboratory cannot analyze urine and blood samples, meaning samples collected by the agency must be sent abroad for analysis under what WADA described as a "strict chain of custody.".

WADA said it continued to monitor RUSADA but had been unable to gain access to the country to review the agency's suspension because of the "ongoing geopolitical situation.".

It added that RUSADA had "collected thousands of samples … including hundreds from weightlifters" so far this year.

"Given the history, WADA remains vigilant when it comes to Russia," James Fitzgerald, WADA's spokesperson, told DW. "We must ensure that no stone is left unturned when it comes to verifying that all the proper testing and other anti-doping activities are taking place.".

Despite being suspended, RUSADA still has the power to investigate and prosecute anti-doping cases involving Russian athletes, which critics find difficult to reconcile.

"It's a compounding problem that WADA is still giving them a free pass when it can't even get into Russia to see what they're doing," remarked Koehler, WADA's former deputy director general.

"There's simply no oversight and no accountability. And quite frankly, I don't think there ever really has been.".

Critics also argue that ongoing questions over RUSADA's leadership and independence suggest that little has been fixed in the decade since the McLaren report.

Even the International Olympic Committee (IOC), whose president, Kirsty Coventry, supports the full return of Russian athletes, has acknowledged a "lack of confidence" over RUSADA's governance.

Nawrocka said the IOC had "recently entrusted" the ITA with an expanded role within Russia in the run-up to the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028, but did not explain what the role would involve or when it might begin.

Sources indicate that in April, investigative outlet The Insider reported that Veronika Loginova, the agency's head, was in a long-term relationship with an alleged FSB officer. The FSB, Russia's domestic security service, played a central role in covering up positive drug tests at the Sochi Games.

Loginova did not respond to questions for this article but dismissed the allegations at the time as "all this nonsense," writing in an email that she believed "sport exists separate from politics.".

WADA confirmed to DW only that its investigations unit was examining the allegations against Loginova and that the inquiry was ongoing.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Joel Lefevre | 26 Nov 2026 01:21, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 01:22.
  • Needing a victory to keep their MLS season alive, the Portland Timbers will host Dallas in game two of that best-of-three series on Saturday at Providence Park.
  • The opener went to Los Toros in Frisco, 3-0, putting them one win away from the Western Conference semi-finals for the first time since 2022.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 26 Nov 2026 01:21, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 01:22.

Needing a victory to keep their MLS season alive, the Portland Timbers will host Dallas in game two of that best-of-three series on Saturday at Providence Park.

The opener went to Los Toros in Frisco, 3-0, putting them one win away from the Western Conference semi-finals for the first time since 2022.

For the second successive campaign, the Timbers face a must-win situation heading into game two of the playoffs after lacking decisiveness in the attacking third last Saturday.

Portland have not made it beyond the opening round of the playoffs since their run to the MLS Cup final in 2021, losing to New York City FC on penalties that year.

They are now 12-10-8 all-time in post-season outings, while winning just one of their last seven playoff games in normal time.

That stated, Marti Cifuentes has seen his side lose just one of their last six league fixtures at Providence Park, winning those last two matches and scoring three goals both times.

In addition to that, this club have gone on to win their last two post-season matches at home, while suffering just one playoff defeat this decade at Providence Park in 90 minutes.

The Timbers have never lost a playoff home game versus Dallas in normal time, though their last post-season win against them at Providence Park occurred in 2015 (3-1).

After a cagey opening 45 minutes in game one, Dallas took command in the second half last week, putting themselves in the driver’s seat to advance.

Whatever Eric Quill is saying to this group at half-time, the message has been well received, with his team outscoring opponents by a combined 6-1 margin in the second half of their last two games.

A triumph on Saturday would snap a three-match MLS winless run for the Texas club away from home and mark their first playoff victory as the visitors since beating the Timbers on penalties in Portland in 2020.

Since that triumph, Dallas have failed to score in four of their last five post-season affairs which took place outside of Frisco.

In 2026, they have conceded in all but three MLS road outings, while allowing three or more goals on four separate occasions.

Los Toros can extend their winning run versus Portland to three matches on Saturday, while they are unbeaten in eight successive meetings against them.

Portland Timbers Major League Soccer form:.

Dallas Major League Soccer form:.

Do not expect to see Juan David Mosquera on the field for the Timbers Saturday as he recovers from a foot and ankle issue, while Zac McGraw has a sore back, Brandon Bye is dealing with a knee injury and Alex Bonetig is doubtful due to a shoulder strain.

Cole Bassett and Kristoffer Velde were the most dangerous Portland players in game one, each with three shots, while James Pantemis made five stops in a losing effort.

At Dallas, Anderson Julio is questionable for this match because of a lower-body injury after sitting out in the opening game of this series.

Joaquin Valiente registered his first career playoff brace in game one, with Sam Sarver scoring his first MLS post-season goal in that victory.

Portland Timbers possible starting lineup:.

Recent findings suggest that pantemis; Hernandez, K. Miller, Waterman, Fory; Bassett, Chara, Da Costa; Velde, Janssen, Lassiter.

Dallas possible starting lineup:.

Daniel; Johansson, Urhoghide, Moore, Norris; Valiente, Kaick, Ramiro, Binyamin; Musa, Sarver.

Dallas tend to sit back away from home, and while their defensive shape will be tough to break down, we believe the Timbers' attacking depth and desperation will keep them alive.

Bloodthirsty Brighton feast on rattled Arsenal

📅 19 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4623 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, overpowered and overrun, Arsenal were subjected to the sort of gruelling treatment they usually inflict on their opponents.
  • According to recent reports, in the biggest test of their season so far, Arsenal fell woefully short of the standards they have set themselves over the past few campaigns.
  • Brighton were everything that Arsenal are expected to be: aggressive, inventive and dominant across the field.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, overpowered and overrun, Arsenal were subjected to the sort of gruelling treatment they usually inflict on their opponents. Mikel Arteta’s side did not look anything like Premier League champions here, as Brighton and Hove Albion produced a stunning performance full of swarming energy and breathless bravery.

According to recent reports, in the biggest test of their season so far, Arsenal fell woefully short of the standards they have set themselves over the past few campaigns. This sort of thing simply does not happen to Arteta’s side. Well, it did not happen. Not before this monstering on the south coast, where the Brighton fans were whipped into a frenzy by the brilliance of Fabian Hürzeler’s players.

Brighton were everything that Arsenal are expected to be: aggressive, inventive and dominant across the field. They even scored with a set-piece, as one of Arsenal’s great strengths became a sudden weakness. Everywhere Arteta looked, the foundational truths of his team were being shaken by a Brighton storm. It was their first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023, also against Brighton.

Remarkably, this is now the third consecutive season in which Brighton have beaten the reigning Premier League champions. They are rarely happier than when they are on the hunt against more illustrious opponents, working as a team to snap at heels and then attacking in numbers. They are known as the Seagulls, but they played more like a pack of bloodthirsty wolves. The ferocity of their off-the-ball work, especially in the first half, was extraordinary.

In a recent development, not for a long time have Arsenal been as rattled as they were here. David Raya misplaced passes, Gabriel Magalhães lost duels and Bruno Guimarães chased the ball in vain. It was Brighton’s Pascal Gross, rather than Arsenal’s Martin Odegaard, who shaped the game in midfield. It was Brighton’s Charalampos Kostoulas, rather than Arsenal’s Kai Havertz, who offered incisive class in attack.

Gross and Kostoulas both struck from range in a one-sided first half, before Chema Andrés added the third after the break. At half-time, Arteta had sprinted down the tunnel towards the dressing room. Whatever messages he gave to his players, they either did not sink in or did not work. By the end, Arsenal were lucky the scoreline was not even more humiliating.

Arteta’s players had come through some tricky assignments in winning their first seven matches of this season, but this was their toughest test yet and they failed it badly. They did not handle the emotions of the occasion particularly well, either: in stoppage time, a frustrated Declan Rice kicked out at Malick Yalcouyé. He was perhaps fortunate to avoid a red card.

It was the first time that Rice and Guimarães had started alongside each other for Arsenal and it swiftly became clear that their £180m partnership will need some work. Arsenal would have hoped their experience in the Premier League would allow for an instant connection but, evidently, that is not the case. Guimarães was hooked after 60 minutes, but might easily have been removed at the break.

Both managers had a similar assessment of the match and how it was won: Brighton did the basics far better than Arsenal. “How we wanted to approach this game was getting into it through small wins,” Hürzeler remarked. “Everyone speaks about a goal or chance as a win, but a small win can be the first throw-in, the first corner, win the first header, win the first tackle. These small things. If you win these small steps, and celebrate them as a win, then you can gain bigger and bigger wins.”.

It was typical of Brighton that one of their new signings produced an excellent performance in midfield. Andrés, a 21-year-old Spaniard signed from Stuttgart at the end of the transfer window, looks to be the latest gem identified by their data-led recruitment model. No one inside the Amex Stadium was thinking about Carlos Baleba, sold to Manchester United, when Andrés made his tackles and won his headers.

Recent findings suggest that another fresh signing, centre-back Luka Vuskovic, was similarly impressive at the back. Signed for £46m from Tottenham Hotspur, Vuskovic looks more than capable of going to the top of the game.

This was perhaps the first occasion this season in which Arsenal missed William Saliba, the injured centre-back who has been so fundamental to their success in recent years. The Frenchman can always be relied on to provide calmness and composure at the back, even under intense pressure. Without him, Arsenal were uncharacteristically jittery.

“The amount of technical errors we did in our own half...” Arteta bemoaned. “We didn’t respect any principle of play that you have to get out of those man-to-man situations. That put us always on the back foot.”.

Gross, who at 35 is playing as well as ever, opened the scoring with a low shot from range after 31 minutes. Kostoulas then struck the second, from a similar distance, after some end-to-end action resulted in Arsenal’s midfield and defence melting away. The third was the most simple, as Andrés headed in at the back post from an inswinging corner.

Arsenal did have some chances, with Havertz missing the best of them, but there was never a sense that Brighton were vulnerable. The pressure on the home side was never sustained. For Arteta, who now has an extended international break in which to ruminate on this defeat, it all made for an unfamiliar and unexpected pain.

Mikel Arteta remarked his Arsenal players failed to “respect the game” as their perfect start to the season was ended in stunning style by a brilliant Brighton performance.

Arsenal’s capitulation on the south coast led to their first defeat of the campaign and Arteta admitted that Brighton had a different “edge” and “bite” throughout the match. The Arsenal manager also remarked the 3-0 loss represented a “substantial lesson” for his players.

Recent findings suggest that “There are certain basics you need to accomplish in football, especially in the Premier League, that we were very far from,” Arteta noted. “From the first throw-in you could sense it, it was so clear.

According to recent reports, “It was a really disappointing result and performance. Brighton were another gear up from us. We were extremely poor technically and were not respecting the game.

Sources indicate that “It is not going to take away what the team has done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup. What we have done and the way we have competed, and the amount of games we have won, has been remarkable. But this is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level.”.

Arteta added that his team did not “respect the principles of play” that were required against Brighton’s intense pressing, and also noted his players were guilty of numerous technical errors.

“Credit to Brighton for what they have done because they have overcome us and they had another edge,” Arteta stated. “There are a lot of moments when the ball is 50/50 and it changes hands and most of the time it was for them.”.

Brighton are the Premier League’s top scorers this season with 16 goals in five matches so far, and this emphatic victory took them up to third place in the table.

“It was a special win,” Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton head coach, said. “Not only because we played the best team in England but because of the performance. I am really proud of my team. It’s always important to enjoy these moments. We were horrible to play against. My players really trust each other on the pitch.”.

In a recent development, two things, one give credit to them. In the manner that they played and committed to every single action. We were below the standards that are required for us but in the Premier League as well.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of today’s Premier League 3pm kick-offs, with Brighton vs Arsenal the pick of the three matches.

Brighton are the league’s top goalscorers so far this season and have amassed the most expected goals, but the champions have the league’s best defence and are seeking five wins from five to start their title defence. There is some welcome needle between Fabian Hurzeler and Mikel Arteta, dating back to Declan Rice’s contentious second yellow for delaying the restart two years ago, as well as the Brighton manager’s comments about Arsenal’s style of play in March.

Recent findings suggest that that 1-0 Arsenal victory at the Amex coincided with Man City dropping points at home to Nottingham Forest on a pivotal night in the title race. Bukayo Saka scored a deflected shot in the ninth minute, and Arsenal held on from there in an ugly but resolute display.

It has been revealed that with Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz fit and firing, as well as the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to Arteta’s midfield stable, Arsenal’s football has been more technical and enterprising so far this season. Brighton are one of the few teams who will back themselves to play through Arsenal’s press, which should make for an absorbing game.

In a recent development, elsewhere, Newcastle are looking to bounce back from their shellacking at Leeds at home to surprise package Hull City. Mattias Jaissle’s team took four points from Liverpool and Spurs but there is concern about how many shots they are conceding. Hull remain unbeaten and continue to confound the odds and underlying data, but that surely cannot last forever.

It has been revealed that everton are also one of the division’s unbeaten teams, but will be targeting three points from a home game against Ipswich after three consecutive draws. Ipswich are sitting comfortably on six points after their win at Crystal Palace, though they did have the extra man for the majority at Selhurst Park.

Full team news on the way shortly.
