The electrically-conducting width of this device is ~12.5 nm. b, Magnified view of the nanocrystalline NbP layer and crystalline Nb seed, together with their corresponding Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), obtained from the boxed regions in panel a. c,d, Bright-field image (c) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental map (d) of the same device, showing distinct material compositions. In total, three NbP (1.5 nm) nanoribbons were examined by cross-sectional STEM. Across these samples, we observe consistent structural and compositional characteristics, including similar NbP crystallinity and sidewall oxidation, which support the scaling behaviour reported in this work. Additional STEM characterization was not performed on thicker NbP nanoribbons, as the thinnest nanoribbons are most relevant to the main conclusions of this study.

It has been revealed that a, HAADF image of the NbP (1.5 nm)/Nb (3.4 nm) nanoribbon with an electrically-conducting width of ~18 nm. b, Magnified view of the nanocrystalline NbP layer and crystalline Nb seed layer, together with their corresponding FFT, obtained from the boxed regions. c,d, Bright-field image (c) and EDS elemental map (d) of the same device, showing distinct material compositions of each region. e, EELS linescan profiles of Nb (blue) and P (red) normalized intensity as a function of position along the direction indicated in panel c. f-h, Representative nanobeam electron diffraction (NBED) patterns extracted from 4D-STEM data at probe positions within the sapphire substrate (f), Nb layer (g), and NbP layer (h), with indexed reflections confirming the distinct crystal structure of each region. i-k, Orientation template matching of the representative NBED pattern in f–h, for the sapphire substrate (i), Nb layer (j) and NbP layer (k). Coloured symbols indicate the local crystallographic orientation of the best-matching template for that pattern. l-n, Phase template matching of the same patterns for the sapphire substrate (l), Nb layer (m) and NbP layer (n).

a, Schematic of the scaling mechanism for conventional metals, with surface scattering and grain boundary scattering. b, As thickness and width of NbP are reduced, the conduction is consistent with the growing dominance of surface carriers, which are disorder-tolerant, with reduced scattering. The total sheet conductance in this case is a sum of the sheet conductance contributed from bulk carriers and surface carriers. c, For thick NbP, bulk carriers dominate the transport, and thus conventional scaling laws apply, with pronounced surface and grain boundary scattering. d, The Fuchs-Sondheimer (FS) and Mayadas-Shatzkes (MS) model fitting of 3.4 nm Nb seed layer, showing an excellent fit. The extracted resistivity with increasing width (W → ∞) is 56.3 μΩ∙cm, which matches the literature results. e, Sheet conductance (GNbP,□) of 1.5 nm NbP as a function of width (red curve), extracted from Fig. 2d of the main text. The sheet conductance from bulk carriers (extracted from Hall measurement) follows the conventional FS-MS scaling model (black dashed line), where the sheet conductance from surface carriers increases as the width decreases due to the increased surface area/volume ratio, as indicated by the purple dashed line. At this ultrathin thickness (1.5 nm), bulk carriers experience strong scattering, resulting in very small bulk carrier sheet conductance. f, GNbP,□ of 10 nm NbP as a function of width (blue curve). At NbP thickness of 10 nm, 3D bulk carriers and 2D top and bottom surface carriers contribute comparably to transport, as shown in Fig. 4b. At this thickness, as the nanoribbon width is reduced, the enhancement in surface conduction is insufficient to offset the increased scattering of bulk carriers. Consequently, bulk transport dominates in this regime, leading to a net reduction of sheet conductance (i.e., increased resistivity) with decreasing width, more similar to conventional metal wires. We note that there could be subtle differences in sidewall roughness and damage in the thicker nanoribbons compared to the thinner ones. See Supplementary Note 2 for the modelling details and more discussion.

Recent findings suggest that a, Bulk Brillouin-zone schematic showing the two mirror planes and nodal rings from the band inversion. b, Representative band dispersion along Γ-S-M’, where the curves calculated without spin-orbit coupling (SOC) show the nodal-ring-related band inversion (plotted in green), and the curves calculated with SOC show the corresponding gap opening (black dashed lines). c, Real-space crystal view highlighting the helical states along the projected mirror line on the surface. d, Surface-state spectrum along \(\overline{\Gamma }\)-\(\overline{{\rm{X}}}\)-\(\overline{\Gamma }\)’, where the narrow Weyl-point window (grey shadow) hosts three pairs of helical states (indicated by arrows) that form the main part of the Fermi arcs, while remnant spin-split surface branches remain visible over a broader energy window (broad green shadow). Blue and red colours indicate the ‘± Sy’ spin polarization at opposite momenta, showing the helical feature. In summary, the narrow Fermi-arc structure is embedded inside a much broader nodal-ring-derived surface-state sector set by the band inversion. See Supplementary Note 7 for more discussion on bulk-topology hierarchy and topological surface-state interpretation.

a, Slab model along the [001] direction for the surface state calculations. Here, the 2 × 2 × 3 supercell is shown as an example. A 4.5 nm thick slab structure of the 1 × 1 × 4 supercell was used in the calculations. b,c, Surface band structures with Nb (b) and P (c) terminations along high-symmetry lines. Blue and red bands indicate the surface states of the Nb and P terminations, respectively. Bulk-projected states shown in pale blue are depicted as the background. The charge neutral point is set to 0 eV. d-f, Surface-projected Fermi surfaces with Nb (upper panels) and P (lower panels) terminations at 0 eV (d), −0.2 eV (e), and −0.4 eV (f). Darker colours represent larger contributions projected from the surface. Weyl points projected on the 2D Brillouin zone are shown as green and purple dots for opposite chirality. The constant energy cuts show surface-dominant open contours over a broad energy window, indicating that Weyl-derived surface bands persist even when the chemical potential is shifted deep into the hole-doped regime, which implies the robustness of the topological surface character. In addition, for the 4.5 nm thick NbP film, the top and bottom surface states exhibit minimal hybridization, except near the Weyl point projections where they meet each other. The Fermi-arc states remain largely unhybridized because they are well separated in momentum space. Even at momenta where they intersect, the resulting hybridization gap is negligible. See Supplementary Note 8 for the modelling details and more discussion.

Sources indicate that a, Slab model from the NbP (001) film with thickness d = 1.5 nm and width W = 4.4 to 5.7 nm. b, The one-dimensional (1D) band structure of a W = 5 nm nanoribbon along ky direction. The edge projection is highlighted in purple to show the edge states, while the bulk states are shown in pale blue. Near EF, the edge-projected subbands form an electron-like pocket, consistent with the negative pedge values (panel f). c-e, The spin projection to Sx (c), Sy (d), and Sz (e) components, respectively, for the edge state. The blue and red represent opposite signs of spin polarization. These edge states exhibit a pronounced spin texture arising from strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in noncentrosymmetric NbP where Sx and Sz components are locked to the ky momentum in a Rashba-type SOC. This reduces the wavefunction overlap between counter-propagating modes, thereby suppressing the leading backscattering channel, which indicates high-mobility edge conduction. f, The carrier densities from edge (pedge) and 2D film (p2D) are extracted from linear fitting of the total ribbon density (p1D) by p1D = pedge + p2DW, at varying W. Wc denotes the cross-over width at which the edge carrier density would dominate the transport over the top and bottom surface carrier density. Here, Wc ≈ 0 indicates that the enhanced edge conduction of ultrathin films is not primarily driven by an increased edge carrier density. Instead, it is more plausibly attributed to an enhanced carrier mobility arising from reduced backscattering as the edge dimension approaches the quasi-1D limit. See more details in Supplementary Notes 2 and 8. g, Agreement between the nanoribbon fitting (\({p}_{2{\rm{D}}}^{{\rm{NR}}}\)) and that obtained from independent slab film calculations (\({p}_{2{\rm{D}}}^{{\rm{slab}}}\)) which corresponds to the d = 1.5 nm thickness in Supplementary Fig. 10. This agreement supports the self-consistency of our calculations across both the nanoribbon and thin-film geometries.

a, Temperature-dependent effective resistivity (ρeff) of NbP films with different thicknesses up to 90 nm, measured from Hall bar devices. These films have a 3.4 nm Nb seed layer, whose resistivity is measured separately (black symbols). b, Low-temperature limit (2-10 K) of panel a. The smallest superconducting transition temperature Tc (~2.2 K) is in the 3.4 nm Nb layer (black symbols), while higher Tc are observed in the NbP/Nb films, and Tc decreases monotonically with thicker NbP. The symbol colours follow the convention in panel a. c,d, Temperature-dependent sheet conductance (GNbP,□) (c) and resistivity (ρNbP) (d) for all NbP thicknesses, after subtracting the Nb seed contribution. e, ρNbP as a function of NbP thickness at 300 K and 10 K. For comparison, the ρNbP values of nanoribbons with the widest widths (Fig. 2d of the main text) are slightly higher than those from Hall measurements at 300 K, possibly due to process-induced damage during nanofabrication. f, Temperature-dependent ρeff of a ~5 nm-thick Nb control film, measured from a Hall bar device. The residual resistivity ratio (RRR) is 1.48, and the Tc is ~4.2 K. Inset: enlarged view of the low-temperature region. The presence of NbP appears to promote superconductivity in NbP/Nb films. The superconducting proximity effect is one plausible interpretation, although changes in disorder and enhanced inter-grain coupling (in the presence of NbP layer) could also contribute. We also cannot fully rule out the formation of an interfacial superconducting layer at the NbP/Nb interface. The NbP sheet conductance is obtained by subtracting the sheet conductance of the Nb layer (measured independently on control Nb films) from the total sheet conductance of the NbP/Nb stack. The extracted NbP resistivity is then obtained by dividing the NbP thickness by the NbP sheet conductance, i.e. ρNbP = dNbP/GNbP,□, where GNbP,□ = Gtot,□ - GNb,□ and Gtot,□ = dtot/ρeff, where Gtot,□ is the total sheet conductance of the NbP/Nb stack, dtot is the total stack thickness and ρeff is the measured effective resistivity (panel a). The GNbP,□ (panel c) represents the NbP sheet conductance after subtracting the independently-measured Nb seed contribution. Additional validation of the subtraction method using Pt/Nb stacks is provided in Supplementary Fig. 19. Control experiments using Pt/Nb stacks validate that the subtraction procedure itself does not generate an anomalous resistivity trend. Nevertheless, the conductance of the Nb seed layer within NbP/Nb stacks cannot be independently measured and it cannot be said, with absolute certainty, that its behaviour is identical to that of the separately measured Nb control film. Thus, the extracted NbP resistivity relies, by necessity, on the model used.

a-c, Hall resistance (Rxy) vs. magnetic field (B) measured at various temperatures for 3.4 nm Nb (a), 1.5 nm NbP (b), and 10 nm NbP (c). For the NbP films (b,c), the Nb seed layer contribution is subtracted at each corresponding temperature to extract NbP Hall response, using the same two-layer Hall conduction model described in the supplement. d, Effective three-dimensional carrier density (p3D) for all films, revealing opposite temperature-dependence: ultrathin 1.5 nm NbP highlights an increasing p3D upon cooling, whereas both thicker NbP (10 nm) and Nb (3.4 nm) display decreasing p3D. (This figure is also included in the main text as Fig. 4d and is reproduced here for convenience). e, Effective hole mobility (μp) of the same films vs. temperature. NbP films exhibit a pronounced increase in mobility upon cooling due to suppressed phonon scattering, whereas the 3.4 nm Nb film shows only a slight rise in mobility, indicating that its transport remains strongly limited by surface scattering.

According to recent reports, a-c, Longitudinal sheet resistance (Rxx) vs. magnetic field (B) measured at various temperatures for films of Nb seed layer (3.4 nm) (a), for NbP (1.5 nm) on the Nb seed (b), and for NbP (10 nm) on the Nb seed (c). All measurements were performed with the magnetic field applied perpendicular to the film plane and current direction. At low temperatures, all films exhibit a pronounced negative cusp near low field regions, arising from the interplay of superconducting fluctuations and weak antilocalization. d-e, Longitudinal sheet resistance (Rxx) vs. magnetic field (B) measured at 1.8 K for both 1.5 nm thick NbP (on 3.4 nm Nb seed layer) and for the Nb layer (3.4 nm) evaluated separately. Measurements were performed with B field perpendicular to the film plane and current direction (d), and with B applied in-plane (e). The superconducting transition temperatures are Tc ~ 6 K for the 1.5 nm NbP (on Nb) and ~2.2 K for the 3.4 nm Nb film (see Fig. 3d of the main text). The upper critical field Hc2, defined as the midpoint between the normal state resistance and zero resistance, is extracted. At 1.8 K, the out-of-plane critical field \({H}_{c2}^{\perp }\) is 2.2 T for NbP (1.5 nm) and 0.38 T for Nb (3.4 nm). The in-plane critical field at 1.8 K exceeds 9 T for NbP (1.5 nm) and reaches 4.44 T for Nb (3.4 nm). The superconducting coherence length estimates are provided in the supplement. The sense current used for Hall bar measurements is 0.5 mA, corresponding to a current density of ~0.1 MA/cm2 for the NbP (1.5 nm) film and ~0.15 MA/cm2 for the 3.4 nm Nb control, with the same 100 μm Hall bar device width. We note that this sense current is well below the superconducting critical current: even when we increased the sense current up to 10 mA, we were unable to suppress the superconducting state at 1.8 K.

Scale bars: 0.5 Å−1. e, EDS line scan across the multilayer stack showing Nb (blue), P (red), and Al (light brown) as a function of position, integrated over a ~ 5nm wide region along the direction indicated by the yellow arrow in panel a, confirming periodic composition and abrupt elemental transitions at each NbP/Nb interface. f-h, denoised NBED patterns from NbP layers 1–3, displaying diffraction symmetry consistent with the NbP crystal structure with indexed reflections, consistent with uniform phase and crystallographic orientation throughout the multilayer stack. The diffraction spots become progressively broader from layer 1 to layer 3, suggesting a gradual decrease in crystalline coherence in NbP layers further from the substrate. This is further supported by the emergence of diffuse ring features in the Layer 3 diffraction pattern, indicative of increasing structural disorder.

#197935. Preparing for 45C: How Germany tests its crisis response

Preparing for 45C: How Germany tests its crisis response

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (745 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Imagine a situation in which prolonged drought has devastated Germany and much of Europe, taking a toll on people's lives, the environment and economy — with a heat wave with temperatures of up to 45 degrees Celsius (113 degrees Fahrenheit) compounding the situation.
  • About 180 organizations across Germany, including more than 60 ministries at the state level and nearly 20 federal authorities, are taking part in a major crisis exercise known as LÜKEX 26, which is built around this very scenario.
  • In a recent development, it is Germany's cross-government crisis management exercise organized by the Federal Office of Civil Protection and Disaster Assistance (BBK).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Imagine a situation in which prolonged drought has devastated Germany and much of Europe, taking a toll on people's lives, the environment and economy — with a heat wave with temperatures of up to 45 degrees Celsius (113 degrees Fahrenheit) compounding the situation.

About 180 organizations across Germany, including more than 60 ministries at the state level and nearly 20 federal authorities, are taking part in a major crisis exercise known as LÜKEX 26, which is built around this very scenario.

In a recent development, it is Germany's cross-government crisis management exercise organized by the Federal Office of Civil Protection and Disaster Assistance (BBK). And it's been up and running for more than two decades.

Recent findings suggest that the first LÜKEX in 2004 dealt with the scenario of an extreme winter with a major power outage. Lessons from that exercise proved valuable in 2005 when the Münsterland region of North Rhine-Westphalia — Germany's most populous state — experienced the worst power outage in the country's postwar history. When heavy snowfall caused power lines to collapse, leaving 250,000 people without electricity for days, there was a better understanding of who to contact and where the bottlenecks were.

Since it first started, LÜKEX has trained for scenarios involving terror attacks, an influenza pandemic, biological health threats, storm floods in northern Germany and gas shortages in southern Germany. The most recent exercise in 2023 simulated a cyberattack targeting government operations.

With the help of other ministries, the German Weather Service and the Federal Institute of Hydrology, the BBK developed a drought risk analysis to serve as the scenario.

Participants, which include aid organizations Malteser and the German Red Cross, didn't know the specifics of the challenges they would be facing until the exercise kicked off on Wednesday.

At that point, they were told it was July 20, 2027. In that simulated future, they find themselves in a Germany that has been struggling with extreme heat for weeks; water levels in rivers are falling, food supplies are becoming scarce and emergency services are under growing pressure.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Patrick Pöhler, spokesperson for Malteser, stated additional details include supermarkets having run out of water, collapsed supply chains and skyrocketing prices to enter a swimming pool. He said the scenario also goes into how the situation is impacting sections of society.

Sources indicate that "Emergency services and elderly care are areas that require particular attention," Pöhler stated. "The increasingly extreme summers of recent years have shown how severely heat can affect staffing levels and operational capacity.".

In its scenario, the northern port city of Hamburg is tasked with managing the disruption of key transport routes that are impacting access to food and drinking water, as well as handling disinformation attacks that are fueling public fear.

It has been revealed that "We have not conducted an exercise of this magnitude since the end of the Cold War. Yet such preparations are essential to strengthen our resilience and crisis-response capabilities," stated Hamburg's minister for the interior, Andy Grote.

LÜKEX is designed to test and strengthen the country's ability to manage major crises at a strategic level. No matter the specific scenario, they all help test internal structures, workflows and decision-making processes.

"The lessons learned are continuously incorporated into improving preparedness, planning and cooperation in civil protection," said BBK spokesperson Katharina Böcker.

This year's topic was decided a long time ago, well before recent summers in which Germany experienced extreme heat, she added. Thousands of people died from heat-related causes during the hot months of this year.

"Crises such as extreme heat waves and prolonged droughts can affect large parts of the population and challenge the operational capabilities of our critical structures over an extended period," mentioned Christian Reuter, secretary general of the German Red Cross, another organization taking part.

Observers take note of how organizations react in the crisis scenario to find out what went well and where things didn't run smoothly.

"We are explicitly encouraged to make mistakes," said Malteser's Pöhler, because that is how weaknesses can be identified and addressed.

A first internal debrief is scheduled for Friday, he added.

Sources indicate that A preliminary report with the main findings and respective recommendations is due to be published in the first quarter of next year. A full evaluation report will then be released later in the third quarter of 2027.

  • Fernandes was a fans’ favourite at Sporting before joining United in January 2020 in a deal worth up to £68million.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 17:50 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 17:54 EST, 24 November 2026.

Bruno Fernandes has left the door open for a return to Sporting Lisbon amid increasing uncertainty over his future at Manchester United.

Fernandes was a fans’ favourite at Sporting before joining United in January 2020 in a deal worth up to £68million.

The United captain has become equally popular at Old Trafford, but returned to Lisbon on Tuesday night with a question mark hanging over his next move after talks over a fresh contract stalled.

Fernandes’ current deal is due to run out at the end of June – and he will be able to speak to foreign clubs from January 1 – although United are expected to trigger an automatic 12-month extension to prevent him from leaving as a free agent in the summer.

Industry observers note that asked if he would consider a move back to the Jose Alvalade Stadium, where United meet Sporting in the Champions League on Wednesday night, Fernandes said: ‘I will never close the door to Sporting. It will always be a club with a special place in my heart.

‘Sporting was the first club that believed in my potential. I’ve always felt here from the fans – regardless of what may have happened – all the love and kindness from them, and that was essential to make me grow as a player.’.

Bruno Fernandes has rejected two offers of a new contract to extend his stay at Man United.

On his future at Old Trafford, Fernandes insisted that he wants to focus on turning United’s season around after they slipped into the relegation zone and replaced head coach Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino.

‘We have time to speak about that,’ remarked Fernandes. ‘I know it's my future and I probably shouldn't look that way because I haven't got long left, but I'm more worried about results.

‘Contract talks have stopped for us to start winning games, and then we can talk about a contract. Now is not the moment.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that mikel Arteta’s press conference takes place early this morning, rather than the typical 1.30pm start time. I woke up a bit later than usual, and there’s part of me that wonders if I should wait for it before doing the blog, but then that would make the blog a lot later than usual and I don’t want to disrupt anybody’s routine. Especially on a Friday.

So, the talking points will come later, if there are any talking points. My guesses on questions today:.

Sources indicate that also, the bloke from Sky Sports will come to the press conference dressed up as a PS5 controller to ask if the manager is concerned about his players staying up all night to to play Grand Theft Auto 6. Hopefully he requires a firmware enhancement before speaking.

It has been revealed that so, in the absence of news and stuff to talk about, I thought I’d point you in the direction of some stuff elsewhere. In a week where we’ve been handing out new contracts all over the place, Phil Costa wonders about the future of Kai Havertz and whether new terms might be on offer for him.

Recent findings suggest that it’s an interesting one because I think it’s clear he’s the manager’s first preference from the two strikers he has available to him. If he was forced to drive deep into the woods and leave one tied to a tree, it’d be Viktor Gyokeres left in the dark forest to try and undo his knots and make his way back to civilisation. But reservations about Kai’s fitness are more than understandable, and while this is a player who has scored major goals for this club since his arrival, there are inconsistencies to his game that can be frustrating.

In a recent development, he turns 28 in June, which is far from over the hill, but it’s then about the cost of a multi-year commitment to a player who, more than likely, you’re probably never going to get much of a return on. Particularly if you have to add to what is already a significant weekly wage packet, even if others will have taken over the mantle of Arsenal’s best-paid player.

Industry observers note that my gut feeling is that we’ll probably keep him though, and jokes aside it probably is connected to Gyokeres. The Swedish international feels like the player most expendable of the two in the manager’s mind, and I just can’t really see any scenario when simply Arsenal hang onto both for another season or two, or decide that both can be sold and then replaced at the same time. We sold two left-wingers and a striker this summer and replaced them with one single player, so it’s not as if our track record of augmenting the squad in forward areas would give you much confidence in our ability to undergo sweeping reform.

It has been revealed that thus, some consistency will be necessary, and if push comes to shove, Arteta will sell Gyokeres a hundred times before Havertz once – unless there’s something to do with fitness/injury. The question then is do we renew now, or see where we are next summer? If we add a younger striker to the mix, the benefit of Havertz’s experience isn’t to be underestimated, and then in those final 12 months, if there’s a deal to be done it can be done, and if not, the club have time to consider other options. At that point, he’ll be almost 29, he’ll have options elsewhere if there’s no future at Arsenal.

Of course players want some security when it comes to their contracts and their futures, it might be a case he wants that and that may force the glitch one way or the other, but as it stands, it doesn’t seem to be an issue that absolutely has to be a top priority right now (unlike someone like Declan Rice, for example).

Recent findings suggest that for more good reading this morning, Lewis writes about Thomas Frank and Mauricio Pochettino (the significant lumpy prick), and the challenges they face with their new clubs. I know I said this on the Arsecast Extra earlier in the week, but I really feel like the latter escapes the scrutiny he deserves for the evil he has perpetrated throughout his career. Manager of Sp*rs, Chelsea and PSG, and now Man Utd, as well as a stint as a national manager during which I thought he thoroughly shamed himself over the Folarin Balogun incident in the World Cup. I know he’s a big mate of Mikel Arteta, but for me he’s up there with the worst of them. A Maroon5 cover of a Phil Collins song brought to life.

Recent findings suggest that right, I’ll leave it there. As I stated yesterday, we’ll have a preview podcast over on Patreon later on, but in the absence of an Arsecast this week we’ll make it available to everyone for free via the usual podcast channels. That should be out after lunch at some time.

Newcastle a challenge but a good post-Interlull opportunity

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (927 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Arseblog

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that arsenal are back in Premier League action after the Interlull with a trip to face Newcastle away from home.
  • Recent findings suggest that in terms of the Arsenal team today, Arteta can flip a coin between Ben White and Jurrien Timber, both of whom were on the scoresheet for their countries during the break.
  • In midfield there’s no Martin Zubimendi whose unfortunate run of injuries continues with a hamstring strain picked up playing for Spain against England.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that arsenal are back in Premier League action after the Interlull with a trip to face Newcastle away from home. It’s been a difficult place to visit over the years, and we’ve had some unenjoyable encounters – there particularly during Eddie Howe’s tenure. However, Mikel Arteta more or less has a full squad to choose from, and this version of Newcastle under newly introduced manager Matthias Jaissle haven’t been at all convincing so far this season.

Recent findings suggest that in terms of the Arsenal team today, Arteta can flip a coin between Ben White and Jurrien Timber, both of whom were on the scoresheet for their countries during the break. My gut feeling is that the Dutchman will start today with White penciled in for Borussia Dortmund in midweek. William Saliba is back after another behind closed doors appearance to build his fitness, but for a game that’s likely to be intense and physical, I can’t see anything other than Ezri Konsa alongside Gabriel today. The Frenchman often needs a game or two to get his rhythm back, and while friendlies are useful, they’re not quite the same as competitive minutes. He too is likely to feature in the Champions League on Tuesday.

In midfield there’s no Martin Zubimendi whose unfortunate run of injuries continues with a hamstring strain picked up playing for Spain against England. The form of Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard means they’re first picks, and then it’s about how the manager views Bruno Guimaraes for a game like this. Even if Newcastle haven’t been great, the pantomime villain in midfield adds a layer of spice that is inevitable after his summer move. If he wants to keep the crowd quiet, he could choose Myles Lewis-Skelly, but he paid £75m for this player for a good reason, and I think we’ll see the Brazilian from the start.

He was a hugely key player for Newcastle, and while I don’t think his departure was among the most contentious we’ve ever seen, he will be a target for their fans, and perhaps for players who know him – and his temper – very well. You’d hope at 28 he’s mature enough to deal with all that, and I’m sure conversations will have been had about not rising to any bait. Arteta has said more than once recently he wants more from this player, where better to give that than his former club?

According to recent reports, as for the front three, I think it will be Christos Tzolis and Noni Madueke either side of Kai Havertz. The injury news for Bukayo Saka means he’s going to miss another month, at least, so there’s a massive onus on Madueke to continue his recent improved form, but we’ll need him to add end product to the one goal and one assist he’s provided in the league so far. Similarly, Tzolis had a bright-ish start to his Arsenal career, and while the hamstring injury was ill-timed, we need a player who is ostensibly our first choice left winger to start delivering more in terms of assists but especially goals.

Recent findings suggest that havertz got the winner away to Liverpool, but had frustrating moments at home to Hull. He’s got Viktor Gyokeres on the bench to put some pressure on him, but this front three has some convincing to do and today would be a very good day to produce performances and end product.

It has been revealed that arteta was asked if the atmosphere at St James’ Park isn’t quite what it used to be, because of the way the team has changed and the inconsistent form they’ve suffered so far this campaign. His message was clear:.

If that’s the case, it will be even more difficult, because they will be even better prepared, they will have even more necessity to do that, and that’s what we expect. We always expect the best version from the opponent. That’s how we have to prepare for the game, and that’s how we’re going to approach it.

So, there’s no chance he’s letting his team think for a second this might be easier because it’s not the same Newcastle that have caused us problems in recent seasons. Nevertheless, he must have looked at this team and some of the concerns they’ve had under their newly introduced manager and recognised that this is an opportunity to go there with a settled side of his own in good form and come away with all three points.

Recent findings suggest that it is always a challenge there, but this is a mature Arsenal that should be capable of dealing with a team that has just three wins from thirteen games in all competitions this season. You never take anything for granted, but if we can keep the ball in the early stages, get control, and perhaps even an early goal, the ingredients are there for us to make this a winning start to what is a tricky run of games over the coming weeks. Fingers crossed.

Right, I’ll leave it there for this morning. As ever, we’ll bring you live blog coverage of the game later, as well all the post-game stuff on Arseblog News like the match report, player ratings, manager reaction, quotes round-up and more. There’s also a preview podcast on Patreon if you need something to listen to ahead of kick off. Don’t forget the updated Arseblog apps also have a cool new matchday centre, full of stats, alerts, and much more.

#197928. Newcastle 2-2 Arsenal: Two points dropped in a game of two halves

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1389 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Arseblog ↗ Open Full Page

Newcastle 2-2 Arsenal: Two points dropped in a game of two halves

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1389 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Arseblog

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, in the cold light of day, it’s hard not to look at what happened in the 45th minute of this game as a key moment.
  • A good move down the left hand side saw Martin Odegaard square perfectly for Noni Madueke who arrived with pace, ready to finish first time.
  • According to recent reports, the lead had come via Eberechi Eze, finishing emphatically after superb work from Kai Havertz to rob the ball and play a deft pass behind the right back.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, in the cold light of day, it’s hard not to look at what happened in the 45th minute of this game as a key moment. Arsenal were 1-0 up, well on top and absolutely deserving of the lead. Newcastle had struggled to exert any kind of control, and we’d already had 9 attempts on goal.

A good move down the left hand side saw Martin Odegaard square perfectly for Noni Madueke who arrived with pace, ready to finish first time. Unfortunately for him and for us, Lewis Hall produced a quite outstanding piece of defending to slide in and block the shot over the bar. That was the difference between Arsenal going in 2-0 up at the break rather than with just the single goal margin.

According to recent reports, the lead had come via Eberechi Eze, finishing emphatically after superb work from Kai Havertz to rob the ball and play a deft pass behind the right back. Newcastle’s only chance had come early, a shot from Jacob Murphy that deflected off his own player and drifted wide with David Raya wrong-footed. After that, we bossed the half, with 11 shots in total, 65% possession, but still only that one goal.

It feels redundant to say this is a very, very good Arsenal team, but if we have a weakness, it’s that we don’t turn this kind of domination into more goals. Very often we don’t need to as our defensive solidity and consistency keeps the opposition at bay, but last night we let our standards slip in that regard, and the lack of firepower or being clinical in the final third came home to roost.

According to recent reports, it was, very literally, a game of two halves. Newcastle made a triple sub at the break and it would be churlish not to give them credit for the fact it made a positive impact. However, the Arsenal performance was night and day. The opposition upped the energy and intensity, and we made mistakes. Odegaard miskicking a Riccardo Calafiori throw-in provided them the opportunity to equalise, and I do wonder why Harvey Barnes was so free at the back post to slide home for 1-1.

That goal gave them momentum, they caused us problems again and again, some of them of our own making with carelessness and misfortune. Eze got back well to defend in our box but unfortunately slipped, Raya’s clearance was unconvincing and then Gabriel had to boot the ball behind for a corner – from which they made it 2-1. Dan Burn drifted off Jurrien Timber to get a free header, the ball scrambled around a bit before Malick Thiaw poked it over the line to give them the lead. Messy, shambolic defending – not very Arsenal at all.

Sources indicate that if we’re being fair, we have to say they could have scored again. David Raya went off with a shoulder injury, Kepa had to make a smart save at the feet of Lewis Miley but why was he one on one with the keeper in the first place? A Joe Willock shot deflected wide in similar fashion to the Murphy one in the first half, and eventually Arteta changed things with Christos Tzolis and Myles Lewis-Skelly coming on for Eze and Bruno Guimaraes who had a quiet return to his former club – bar that first half moment when he almost got enough contact on a fantastic Declan Rice cross but could only put the ball wide from close range.

We did get an equaliser, and very well worked it was too. We played the ball across the back line from right to left, into midfield where Havertz’s smart dummy allowed Odegaard room to drive on and find Madueke. He was Arsenal’s best attacking player last night, he kept trying to make things happen, and while I think the Newcastle keeper will probably have nightmares about letting that shot in, Madueke deserved the goal, and it earned us a point.

It was after the 90th minute when the manager brought on Viktor Gyokeres and Mikel Merino to try and find a winner, the Swede had one shot over the bar from the edge of the box, but had we found another, it would have been a real smash and grab. In the end, the draw was probably a fair result based on how the game played out, and afterwards the manager was unhappy at leaving two points behind:.

My feeling is that we have lost two points today. And I say we because we were exceptional in the first half, from the beginning to the end. It should have been two, three or four-nil up, clear. But it wasn’t.

Industry observers note that we started to lose duels, we started to lose second balls. We gave the ball away and have really poor circulation balls against their press and their waves. And when that happens, you give them belief.

It’s a pity because the margin should have been, again, much bigger for the level that we’ve shown.

According to recent reports, and this is the key for me. It should have been, but it wasn’t, and it too often isn’t. As I said above, our defensive brilliance is fundamental to us winning so many games, but football is a game of variance. You can’t always control everything. On another night Odegaard just puts his foot through that throw in and that first Newcastle goal doesn’t happen. Eze and Raya deal better with that situation and we don’t concede a corner. We can focus on those individual things and say we could and should do better for sure, but you have to allow for some of that over the course of a season. You cannot be perfect for 90+ minutes 38 games in every league campaign.

It has been revealed that the ongoing concern for me is our firepower though. I thought generally the front three played pretty well last night, and it’s not as if we missed a glut of chances, but it’s about turning the level of dominance we had in that first half into more goals. This isn’t a one-time issue either. We scored two lovely goals last night but we should have had that game firmly in our grasp at half-time, but in this league a single goal margin is never a sure thing.

The summer was a let-down in an attacking sense, there’s no getting away from that. If we had a forward line that was even close to our midfield and defence in terms of quality and depth, the Premier League would be a cakewalk. I know that’s a bit simplistic, but it’s also a fact. Regardless of what you think of the business, we let goals go to Turkey and Saudi Arabia, and replaced them with a player who has yet to score. Which isn’t to lay the blame at the feet of Tzolis, far from it, but with the squad planning/building that was undertaken.

For me, January becomes increasingly important because the improvement required is obvious, and for a sporting director whose track record looks quite hit and miss as it is, he needs a convincing window or the questions around the job he’s doing will become louder and louder, and for good reason.

The other big concern from yesterday was the injury to David Raya. It didn’t look good at all, and any absence for him would be a huge blow to the team. He’s been the best in the Premier League, and perhaps the best in Europe, for the last 18 months, and inevitably there’s a drop-off when any club is without their first choice keeper for any period of time. That’s another adjustment we’re probably going to have to make, and if it means we’re likely to be less secure and clean sheets are harder to come by, then that issue of scoring goals and being more potent comes into even sharper focus. Let’s keep fingers crossed it’s not as bad as it appears to be.

In a recent development, right, I’ll leave it there for now. There’s plenty to unpick from this one, so I’ll leave you to it in the Arses. More here tomorrow, including an Arsecast Extra. Until then, have a great Sunday.

Juventus Next Gen beaten 4-0 at Lecco and left third from bottom

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Juventus Next Gen were beaten 4-0 at Lecco in Serie C Girone A, with three of the goals coming after half-time.
  • At the Stadio Rigamonti-Ceppi, the manner of the defeat was as worrying as the scoreline.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Juventus Next Gen were beaten 4-0 at Lecco in Serie C Girone A, with three of the goals coming after half-time. Coach Massimo Brambilla admitted his young side give goals away too easily, and the table now reflects a long poor run.

At the Stadio Rigamonti-Ceppi, the manner of the defeat was as worrying as the scoreline.

In a recent development, the opener set the tone. Lecco needed only six minutes to go ahead. Casarotto ran through the middle, got past Corradi and beat goalkeeper Mangiapoco. Lecco held that single-goal lead until half-time.

Next Gen did have one clear opening before the break. In the 40th minute, Grelaud shot from near the penalty spot. Vettorel turned the effort over for a corner.

The second half was one-way traffic. Capello made it 2-0 in the 50th minute, and Manetti added a third in the 56th. Capello struck from close range after the goalkeeper parried Pellegrino’s second attempt. Murillo’s goal in the 72nd minute summed up the match. Mangiapoco erred as Juventus built from the back, and Murillo pounced.

Industry observers note that the hosts are in strong form. This was their second 4-0 win in a row, after beating Dolomiti Bellunesi by the same score. Lecco have now scored 15 goals in four games.

Massimo Brambilla did not hide from the problems. He told TuttoMercatoWeb that his side struggled against Lecco’s high press. His players found it hard to keep the ball against a team pressing hard and man-to-man.

The coach also admitted that coming back became difficult after the second goal. He mentioned his players must improve how they read the game and stop giving away goals so easily.

In a recent development, the table makes the warning sharper. Brambilla’s side sit third from bottom after the defeat, having won just one of their last 12 matches.

In a recent development, the result also matters beyond Serie C. Carnevali has put the youth sector at the centre of the club’s intends.

One player supporters will watch is Destiny Elimoghale, who came off the bench at Lecco. Next Gen had started in a 3-5-2, with Durmisi and Merola in attack. Elimoghale replaced Durmisi in the 40th minute of the second half. The forward was born in 2009. His latest contract, announced on 3 November, runs until 30 June 2029.

Elimoghale was called up to the first-team squad for the first time on 17 September 2026. That call-up came for the opening Europa League league-phase match against NEC.

The next opponents arrive in good spirits. Treviso beat Novara 2-0 in round 13. Romeo scored in the 24th minute, and Paganini added the second in the 59th.

The next test comes quickly. Next Gen host Treviso in round 14 on Sunday 15 November at 17:30. A trip to Giana Erminio follows on Saturday 21 November, at the same kick-off time.

#197926. Mind the gap

Mind the gap

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (902 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Arseblog

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Over the last few weeks, I’ve grown accustomed to waking up and experiencing low-level fear first thing in the morning.
  • Recent findings suggest that with any team or any squad there are players whose absence will be more keenly felt than others, but one of the things Arsenal have generally done really well in the last few years is close the gaps between ‘first choice’ and those behind them.
  • If Jurrien Timber is out, we have Ben White.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over the last few weeks, I’ve grown accustomed to waking up and experiencing low-level fear first thing in the morning. Today, it was a nice change not to be focused on my own health, and instead for my anxiety to centre around someone else – David Raya.

Recent findings suggest that with any team or any squad there are players whose absence will be more keenly felt than others, but one of the things Arsenal have generally done really well in the last few years is close the gaps between ‘first choice’ and those behind them. It doesn’t mean there isn’t still a kind of hierarchy, just that you’re better able to cope if injury or suspension hits. Mikel Arteta referencing ‘finishers’ rather than substitutes might be a psychological ploy to keep his squad happy, but it’s more easy to apply when you have the group of players he has at his disposal.

If Jurrien Timber is out, we have Ben White. If Riccardo Calafiori can’t play, Piero Hincapie can. We all worried about William Saliba needing a long lay-off after the World Cup, but the arrival of Ezri Konsa offset that in exemplary fashion. If we miss Declan Rice, we have two World Cup winners, a Brazilian international, and one of the most highly regarded young English midfielders around to fill that gap. Further forward, Noni Madueke is performing at a level that makes Bukayo Saka’s absence feel less impactful than it would have previously, and while I think forward line quality remains an issue we need to solve as urgently as January, you can flip a coin between most of our options there without feeling you’ve weakened yourself considerably.

It has been revealed that unfortunately, I don’t think the same applies between the sticks. Raya has been the stand-out goalkeeper of the last few years, establishing himself as Arsenal’s number 1 after an initial settling in period. One, by the way, which I don’t think the manager handled particularly well. Typically he’s been near flawless in terms of his man-management, and while he was fundamentally right about wanting the Spaniard to come in and take the position to a new level, the way he fudged things around Aaron Ramsdale, talking about how he’d sub a goalkeeper in a game and all that nonsense really wasn’t his best moment. It left both of his keepers in a weird place for too long, until Raya’s confidence grew and his quality came to the fore.

Industry observers note that since then he’s won multiple golden glove awards, his shot-stopping has been incredible at times, and although every player and every keeper will make mistakes, his have been few and far between. For me though, despite the eye-catching acrobatics – which are more easily clipped up for the social media generation – his key asset is the assurance he brings to the team. Not just when he has the ball at his feet (even if there are times I would like him to move it more promptly), but how good he is from opposition set-pieces and crosses. He comes and claims and eases pressure time and time again, and I think that’s the thing we’re going to miss most if he’s out for any significant period of time.

Kepa is obviously a very experienced second choice, but is second choice for a reason. Realistically though, I don’t think there’s much any club can do to have a back-up option that’s nearly as good as their number 1. If you’re being brutally honest, many clubs in the Premier League don’t have a first choice that comes anywhere close to be as good as Raya, despite their best efforts and spending millions to try and find that player. So, as anxious as I am about him being out, it is one of those things we can’t really complain about. We just have to get on with it.

Industry observers note that as I stated in yesterday’s blog, we are probably going to be less secure at the back, that feels kind of inevitable, so the onus on the players further forward increases. Score more goals, turn that domination of possession and territory into more chances. If we have the ball in their half, our goalkeeper becomes something of a non-problem for as long as that’s the case. There are ways to cope, but we might need to gird our loins for some iffy moments at the back that we haven’t had to experience too often of late.

Sources indicate that as Arsenal fans though, we’ve come through worse than this with goalkeepers in the past. I don’t want to give anyone PTSD first thing on a Monday morning, but when you’ve lived what we’ve lived in seasons gone by, hopefully a little Kepa period won’t be too traumatic. And maybe, after the scan, there’ll be better news about Raya than we expect. Fingers crossed.

Sources indicate that right, I have to leave it there for this morning. We will have an Arsecast Extra for you a bit later on though. We’ve already put out the call for questions on BlueSky @gunnerblog.bsky.social and @arseblog.com, so fire away using the hashtag #arsecastextra – or if you’re an Arseblog Member on Patreon, leave your question in the #arsecast-extra-questions channel on our Discord server.

Industry observers note that pod should be out around noon. Until then!

The Lilywhites have returned to the top half of the Premier League table as a result, and De Zerbi now seeks a slice of revenge after suffering a 1-0 defeat to Sunderland in his Tottenham debut last season.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up all of Tottenham's latest injury and suspension news ahead of their meeting with the Black Cats, who are 18th in the rankings with nine points from 11 games.

Industry observers note that possible return date: November 29 (vs. Sunderland).

Sandro Tonali was absent from last Saturday's win over Ipswich due to illness, but he has returned to Tottenham training and is expected to be available for the weekend.

Savio returned from a muscular injury as a second-half substitute against Ipswich, but the Brazilian attacker then had to come off with a similar concern towards the end.

The severity of Savio's latest concern is not clear, but there is little to no chance of him facing Sunderland.

Possible return date: November 29 (vs. Sunderland).

Tosin Adarabioyo had made a full recovery from a calf injury before last weekend's triumph, but he was not risked by De Zerbi.

Possible return date: December 6 (vs. Arsenal).

Possible return date: February 20 (vs. Brighton & Hove Albion).

Xavi Simons is almost seven months into his recovery from an ACL rupture, and all being well, the Dutchman could make his comeback in mid to late February.

Sources indicate that possible return date: February 6 (vs. Ipswich Town).

Likewise, Wilson Odobert will not play again in 2026 due to his own serious knee injury, but De Zerbi is hopeful that the winger will return to full training in January ahead of a potential February return.

Possible return date: December 6 (vs. Arsenal).

De Zerbi revealed last week that Mathys Tel will need another "two or three weeks" to recover from the ankle injury he picked up against Leeds, so the Frenchman could be targeting a comeback for the North London derby on December 6.

Tottenham have no players banned for this game.

#197923. England throw it away with defending unworthy of a top nation

England throw it away with defending unworthy of a top nation

📅 26 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 32 min read (6420 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~32 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that there had been so much talk – first raised by Thomas Tuchel after the shocking World Cup exit to Argentina – about England’s DNA.
  • Recent findings suggest that the world and European champions were England’s first opponents – after the World Cup – in this Nations League campaign and came away from Wembley with a deserved win.
  • Sources indicate that mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that there had been so much talk – first raised by Thomas Tuchel after the shocking World Cup exit to Argentina – about England’s DNA. About whether they could keep the ball, pass the ball, control the ball, the way Spain do.

Recent findings suggest that the world and European champions were England’s first opponents – after the World Cup – in this Nations League campaign and came away from Wembley with a deserved win. They are now 39 games unbeaten with substitute Mikel Oyarzabal, who scored the winning goal against England in the final of the last European Championship, doing so again.

Sources indicate that mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN! 🎯Spain retake the lead after a slick finish from the Spaniard 👏#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pPT3KvRHWl.

That may have been no surprise, even if the inevitable “olés” after Spain’s third goal will have hurt. But the nature of it? For the England manager this was another shocker. Not in the way his team went about the task. They were positive, fun, attacking. But in the way they conceded – goals and chances – and lost.

According to recent reports, on this performance, DNA, for England, stands for Defensively Not Able, as they threw away what could have been a famous and restorative victory. Instead, with Croatia beating the Czech Republic in the other group game, England are under immediate pressure to win in Prague on Tuesday.

In fact, England have conceded 13 goals in their past six matches – in fairness including four in that third-place World Cup 6-4 win over France – and that is not good enough for a top-tier nation. Tuchel needs to sort it out defensively.

It could have been very different if Harry Kane had not missed from the penalty spot, slipping as he struck the ball, with England improbably 2-1 ahead. “It would have been the decisive punch,” Tuchel stated. Maybe so, even if there was always the feeling that Spain could go through the gears.

It has been revealed that kane MISSES from the penalty spot! 😧Harry Kane slips when he strikes the ball, let off for Spain and Luis de la Fuente#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pvg3GGa9ma.

Afterwards there were claims, led by the impressive Anthony Gordon, that this was a missed opportunity for England. A bit like the World Cup. They need to shake this theme.

The irony was this was one of their best creative displays for quite some time. They took the game to Spain and could have scored more. And conceded more.

In truth it could have been Spain 4 England 0 inside half an hour and before Tuchel’s team laid a glove on their opponents.

Another let off for England 😧Ferran Torres misses another significant chance one-on-one with James Trafford #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/KFkJoJUW6c.

Recent findings suggest that the manager had also spoken about how England should “embrace the chaos” as their best route to success. That may appear a questionable tactic – does chaos ever win a tournament? – but England certainly did that. This was as chaotic and, admittedly, entertaining as it gets.

England attacked with pace and power with the pick of their players the two based in Spain: Gordon, who scored, and Jude Bellingham. And the defenders? This was a bad night for Marc Guéhi, his Manchester City team-mate Nico O’Reilly (cue speculation about whether they were distracted by the verdict on the Premier League charges against their club) and for Jarell Quansah at right-back who is so evidently a centre-half.

A penny, once more, for the thoughts of the unused Trent Alexander-Arnold. The fourth defender, Ezri Konsa, vented his frustration at what was happening around him.

Sources indicate that it was not just the errors but the unforced nature of them. Poor in possession with misplaced passes and defensively wide open. There is a gap between Spain and England but not as massive as the gaps that were exposed in England’s back four. They endured a full house of calamities. They seemed strangely unaware – or incapable of dealing with – the danger posed by the outstanding Lamine Yamal.

Maybe because of the opposition – or the criticism – England felt the need to play out. But what an horrific start. What an inexplicable moment for Guéhi as he received the ball from O’Reilly and turned into trouble, gifting possession to Yamal who ran on and scored. Inside two minutes.

WHAT A START FROM SPAIN 🇪🇸Lamine Yamal pounces on a Marc Guéhi error to give Spain an early lead at Wembley #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/Et83EyTPlp.

It has been revealed that spain walked out with the second star on their shirt – to mark their second World Cup triumph. That was the star Tuchel had promised for England.

Recent findings suggest that now, straight away, they were up against it. It could have turned very ugly. Ferran Torres, who had scored the winner in the World Cup Final, had one disallowed for offside, then was thwarted by James Trafford after – inexplicably again – being played onside by Quansah.

BIG SAVE from James Trafford 🧤The Leeds United goalkeeper keeps out Ferran Torres#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/nj5b8AUSQU.

Then Torres was sent clear following Elliot Anderson’s poor pass, only to drag his shot wide. The third miss came from Dani Olmo, again set up by Yamal.

Recent findings suggest that it could – it should – have been game over. Then England unexpectedly turned it around. They had kept attacking despite what was going on at the back and struck through a truly thrilling counter-attack, with Gordon and Bellingham combining before the Barcelona winger calmly beat goalkeeper Unai Simon.

In a recent development, ENGLAND ARE LEVEL! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿A brilliant finish from Anthony Gordon after a breathtaking counter attack 👏#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/z0nSfWIHVd.

It was an exceptional goal and was promptly followed by a fortunate one as O’Reilly’s cross was met by Kane who stooped to steer in a header, only for it to strike Marc Cucurella, who made a mess of clearing, and it went past Simón.

I think we'll give that goal to Harry Kane 🎯England come from behind to lead Spain thanks Harry Kane, with assistance from Marc Cucurella ⚽️#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/X3qSOWUhVT.

The Spain left-back hit the post with a cross, misjudged by Trafford who was given this game and the next to stake his claim ahead of Jordan Pickford who has so long been the undisputed first-choice.

England dominated for a while and Bellingham won a penalty, after a VAR intervention, only for Kane to strike the crossbar.

In a recent development, how Spain made them pay and worryingly so. O’Reilly passed the ball straight to Olmo who swept it inside. Substitute Álex Baena checked and beat Trafford from the edge of the area. Even worse was how Spain cut through the heart of England defence with Baena finding Oyarzabal. Why was no defender closer to him? What was Guéhi doing? And O’Reilly? Oyarzabal exquisitely dinked the ball over Trafford.

Thomas Tuchel does not think Manchester City’s guilty verdict over almost all of their Premier League charges distracted his England players in the Nations League defeat to Spain.

City players Marc Guéhi and Nico O’Reilly were at fault for two of Spain’s goals and both Tuchel, the head coach, and England captain Harry Kane confirmed news of the verdict had been discussed among the squad.

Tuchel does not strategy to address the matter with his players ahead of the remaining Nations League games against Czech Republic and Croatia.

It has been revealed that asked if the City verdict had been a cause of discussion ahead of the Spain game, Tuchel replied: “Not for me, but I can imagine maybe for the Man City players. I won’t comment on it as it’s an ongoing case.

In a recent development, “I didn’t make it a topic. It was not a topic for me. I’m just thinking about Spain and the team and meetings. The players have more time than me. So I can imagine they talk about it. It’s good they do. I don’t think it was a distraction for them.”.

Kane added: “There was a discussion, but when we’re with England, we kind of put club football to one side and it was no different this week.”.

Tuchel also refused to point the finger of blame at Guéhi, O’Reilly or Kane, who missed a penalty, for England’s defeat despite admitting his team got off to the worst possible start by conceding a goal after two minutes.

“We will focus on the positives, but also highlight the stuff we can do better,” Tuchel noted. “Not even speaking about individual mistakes because this is normal. It just happens. It should not happen, and for sure not in this amount. But there is no sense in showing the individual mistakes or telling them ‘please don’t make mistakes’. That is normal, but we can do things better. We can defend the third goal better. But we will focus on the positives. There is a lot to take away from the game.

It has been revealed that “We wanted to be the team desperately to beat them [Spain] and we think we had them. We still think we had them at half-time. That was the way the team showed up after half-time. So we will focus on that, but the reality is we lost and the reality is we need to prove it again.”.

In a recent development, “It was a terrible start, the worst possible start, which makes it so difficult against a team like this. The reaction was very good. After 10/12 minutes, we were the better team but we gave away too many mistakes. We were the better team. If we had converted the penalty, it could have been the decisive moment. We have to keep going and learn from the mistakes. We could have created more if we had been more clinical in the final 20 metres. We showed great bravery and courage with our high-ball wins. There will always be moments you suffer against teams like this. The effort and quality were there tonight but the result does not prove it today.”.

In a recent development, “I think there is a gap [between Spain and England]. They [Spain] are the world champions and European champions. Mikel Oyarzabal was never going to miss. He was always in control of the situation. Honestly, people talk about sexy football, that is sexy football. I would watch that all night.”.

🗣️ "We went toe to toe with the European and world champions" 💪Harry Kane remains positive about England performance despite their 3-2 defeat to Spain 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿🇪🇸#ITVFootball | @gabrielclarke05 | @England pic.twitter.com/qkhqsqmPEl.

🗣️ "You have to beat them to show people we can do this" 💪@IanWright0 reflects on England's 3-2 defeat to Spain at Wembley#ITVFootball | @markpougatch pic.twitter.com/ko2FYs4VqA.

According to recent reports, marc Guehi and Nico O’Reilly may want to look away now but Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon scored well. Our very own Mike McGrath has provided his player ratings.

Tonight: England 2 Spain 3 (H)Tuesday September 29: Czech Republic (A), kick-off 7.45pmSaturday October 3: Croatia (A), kick-off 5pmTuesday October 6: Czech Republic (H), kick-off 7.45pm.

🗣️ "I think it's a bit of a missed chance" 👀Anthony Gordon says mistakes cost England the win tonight against Spain at Wembley 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @gabrielclarke05 | @England pic.twitter.com/AJBxVNjbjq.

A highly entertaining game. England will probably argue the game changed on Kane’s missed penalty, but Spain missed a lot of very clear chances and will feel they deserved the victory. A losing start to the Nations League for Tuchel and his team, but there were some positives. Gordon, Bellingham and Anderson were all excellent. Some of the defending, not so excellent.

Possession: England 47%-53% SpainShots: 13-15Shots on target: 5-5Corners: 6-3Touches in opposition box: 37-15.

England have one last chance with a corner out on the left. This will be it. Spain are able to deal with it and clear their lines.

Industry observers note that then comes the final whistle at Wembley and the world champions Spain claim a 3-2 victory in north London. It was an absorbing game, where momentum swung one way and then the other, but it is Spain who are the victors.

According to recent reports, baena brings down Rogers with a silly challenge to gift England a free-kick deep in the Spanish half. This could be England’s last chance.

Anderson is over it but his delivery is poor, easily caught by Unai Simon.

England are running out of time to find an equaliser.

O’Reilly appears to be suffering with cramp but England have made all five substitutions.

There will be five added minutes.

A late change for England as Branthwaite replaces Guehi.

Rogers delivers a dangerous cross from the right that runs through the six-yard box and forces Pubill to put it behind for a corner.

England take it short before Anderson clips it in but Laporte heads away.

In a recent development, garner should have done so much better with that. His run into the Spain box on the left side is picked out by Anderson’s pass. Garner has Calvert-Lewin waiting at the back post but the former massively overhits the cross.

Double substitution from England as Calvert-Lewin and Gibbs-White replace Kane and Saka. Rare to say Kane taken off, especially when England are behind.

It has been revealed that saka goes down under a challenge from Cucurella inside the Spain penalty box but no penalty is forthcoming. VAR has cleared the incident. Moments later, Bellingham is then booked for stopping Spain going on the counter.

Spain make a change as Merino replaces Olmo.

The way Spain control possession and keep the ball is impressive. They toy with you pretty well and often look so composed.

Baena, who has been superb since coming on, feeds a lovely pass into the path of Oyarzabal on the right side of the box. Oyarzabal takes one touch before lifting it over Trafford into the England net. That is a lovely assist from Baena and lovely finish from Oyarzabal.

Sources indicate that mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN! 🎯Spain retake the lead after a slick finish from the Spaniard 👏#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pPT3KvRHWl.

Industry observers note that given the quality of the opposition and the sustained threat he carried, that might have been Gordon’s best-ever performance in an England shirt. Him and Bellingham have been excellent. But now he’s been replaced by Morgan Rogers.

Sources indicate that guehi joins O’Reilly in the book for a cynical foul on Olmo. You can put that yellow card in the category of a professional foul.

Harry Kane wants England to address how they lost their identity and went “against our beliefs” at the World Cup.

In a brutally honest assessment of the tournament, the England captain admitted Thomas Tuchel’s team did not play to their full potential in several games – even before the painful semi-final exit against Argentina.

Kane, who played golf instead of watching the World Cup final, revealed the 2-1 Atlanta defeat hurt more than missing a penalty four years earlier in Qatar, when England were knocked out by France in the quarter-finals.

“This one hurt more than any other one. I would probably say even more than when I missed a penalty in Qatar because of the manner that it happened,” Kane stated. “It was not us as a team.

“We trust our players and the player know very well that if you miss a camp then someone plays well in your position that the competition is always on. You have to make sure to be available and to produce top-level performances in camp and if you do so, that counts for something. Right now, it is not on my list of worries. I am not wired like this. From the moment I arrived at SGP my full focus is 100 per cent with the players who are here.

It has been revealed that “There is no threat, distrust or threat of consequences. It will come naturally. I truly believe that we have the opposite. You will talk to our captain, Harry Kane, who has the most minutes for club and country and is happy to be here while teammates of his are enjoying a 10-day break. He is the role model and that is the vibe we have here.”.

They do have plenty to cheer about:.

James Trafford is poised to start for England ahead of Jordan Pickford against Spain tonight.

Pickford has been England’s No1 for eight years but Thomas Tuchel is set to make a change to face the world champions in the Nations League opener at Wembley.

Trafford went to the World Cup in the summer and has started the Premier League in good form following his move to Leeds.

In the first match since the World Cup, changing his goalkeeper is a major selection decision from Tuchel.

Elsewhere, Jarell Quansah is set to play at right-back ahead of Trent Alexander-Arnold while Myles Lewis-Skelly is also in line to return to the starting XI after being recalled into the squad after missing the World Cup.

In a recent development, england begin their Nations League campaign with a home game against the world champions Spain. This is England’s first game since the World Cup, with their dreams of glory ended by Argentina in the semi-finals, but they did finish third after beating France in a high-scoring third/fourth play-off. The last meeting between these sides saw Spain beat England to win Euro 2024. They also faced off in the Nations League back in 2018, with Spain winning at Wembley and England taking victory over in Spain.

In a recent development, england’s looks for these games has been disrupted by a number of withdrawals. Cole Palmer had earned a recall having been left out of the World Cup squad but the Chelsea forward has withdrawn due to a minor injury, despite playing the full game for Chelsea against Brentford in the final game before the international beak.

“He [Palmer] plays with discomfort and pain and cannot play on the highest level with discomfort and pain,” Tuchel noted. “Chelsea informed us. That is my understanding. We are not managing load. This is not an ‘international break’. It is a competitive environment, where the players love to train and be together. That is what we created. We will never compromise on that. We will never let this feeling creep in that the players do not want to come [to England camps]. We focus on the guys who absolutely want to play for England.

Industry observers note that “For sure it is a missed opportunity. It is another missed opportunity. He misses too many opportunities. I do not blame him for it, it is just a fact. He misses way too many camps with injuries. I only want to rely on what I personally witness and see within my team. For that you have to be in camp. If you are not in camp there is a next level to impress that you cannot achieve because you can only do it with me on the pitch and with us on the pitch. It is a missed opportunity.”.

Declan Rice has also withdrawn from the squad despite playing the full game in Arsenal’s defeat to Brighton as have Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento. Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner have been called up as a result.

According to recent reports, trent Alexander-Arnold is back in the fold for the first time since June 2025. 18-year-old Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha made his England debut against New Zealand during the World Cup warm-ups and takes his place in this squad, although he does make the matchday squad for tonight’s game. England will also take on Czechia, Croatia and then Cezchia again during this international break.

Having been crowned world champions back in July, Spain are now champions of both Europe and the world. Back in June 2025, Spain made the Nations League final but lost on penalties to Portugal. Ahead of this international window, The Royal Spanish Federation has extended Luis de la Fuente’s contract until 2032. After tonight, Spain will host Croatia and Czechia before travelling to Croatia to cap off this international window.

It has been revealed that this is an extended international break, with four games to take place during this window. Team news from Wembley to follow shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla owner Elon Musk noted on Friday that the company would scale down production of the Cybertruck at its Austin factory in the coming year.

The South African entrepreneur said Tesla would be scaling back production of his futuristic but often-mocked pickup truck and amping up production of what he hopes will soon become a fleet of fully automated taxis.

"Tesla will be winding down production of the cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production," Musk said on his X social media site.

The announcement follows a bruising week for Musk amid the US midterm elections, where Republicans struggled despite his major donations, with his companies losing billions in value by market capitalization as investors sought to ditch stock.

Musk later responded to a complimentary user online who hailed the Cybertruck as the "best vehicle Tesla has ever made," and calling it an "end of an era" by saying: "True.".

For years he had poured much of his enthusiastic marketing zeal into promoting the Cybertruck, saying during the 2023 launch "finally, the future will look like the future.".

However the oversized body, straight lines and stainless steel and the post-apocalpytic vibe these created also met with widespread criticism and even mockery.

The electric powertrain was probably a barrier to sales in the US, by far the biggest pickup truck market, where Musk had hoped to take on some of the country's top-selling gas-guzzling vehicles like the Ford F150 or the Chevrolet Silverado and the Dodge Ram.

Meanwhile, the car's striking shape, weight and size made it impossible for Tesla to try to crack Europe, where electric vehicles are gaining a much larger market share.

Industry observers note that unlike in the US, EU safety regulations place considerable emphasis not just on people in cars in accidents, but also on the dangers posed to pedestrians who might be hit by a vehicle. That meant it was not possible for Tesla to register and sell the Cybertruck for road use in Europe.

Beyond this, the vehicle's size would likely have rendered it impractical and unpopular on many European roads, where space tends to be at more of a premium.

Depending how quick the wind-down proves to be, the Cybertruck's production run could prove shorter than its five-year R&D phase.

Given its longstanding issues meeting Musk's very public sales and production predictions, Tesla does not publish sales figures broken down by model.

But according to the automotive data platform Kelley Blue Book, the tech giant sold 20,237 Cybertrucks in the US last year, down from 38,965 in 2024.

At launch in 2023, Musk had predicted unit sales nearer a quarter of a million.

For orientation, Ford sold more than 800,000 F-Series pickups in the US last year, a slight boost on 2024's numbers. These vehicles start at less than half the list price of a Cybertruck in the US.

According to recent reports, the IPO for SpaceX this year revealed that Musk's second-largest manufacturer was comfortably the biggest buyer of Cybertrucks in 2025. It bought vehicles worth $131 million and did not even enjoy a bulk-buy or friends-rate discount, paying list prices for the fleet.

The Cybercab is a vehicular element in Musk's bid to transform Tesla towards a manufacturer focused more on AI and robotics than automobilies.

Rather than just featuring the self-drive or driving assistance programs that Musk has been championing for years, the Cybercab has no steering wheels, pedals or mirrors at all and is designed never to have a human in control.

Musk say the model will be the company's main autonomous model and will supply a global network of Robotaxis.

Starting in the past few months, around 300 such vehicles have been registered and have started operating, on approved roads in the Austin area near Tesla's Gigafactory Texas. They're being added to the existing fleet of autonomous Model Y Teslas being used for the purpose, serving in an area known as a geofence of around 680 square kilometers (264 square miles).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Welcome to another Arsecast Extra, the Arsenal podcast, with myself and James from @gunnerblog.

In this Interlull episode we look back on Saturday’s 2-2 draw with Newcastle at St James’ Park. We chat about an impressive first half from Arsenal, taking a deserved lead into the break through Eberechi Eze’s fine goal, but should that dominance and control have brought a bigger lead? We then try to figure out how and why things went so wrong in the second half, falling behind as Newcastle scored twice due to our own carelessness, before Noni Madueke capped a good performance with a very well worked equaliser. Was this a point rescued or two points dropped? After the break we have listener questions about how we cope with a potential David Raya absence after he came off with injury, Bruno Guimaraes and his impact so far in red and white, potential rotation in midweek for Borussia Dortmund, the player ratings question from last week and much more besides.
